mapName: A Learnable World - Identify Every Country

metas.name: Alaska - License Plates
metas.note:
• The most common and recognisable Alaskan licence plate is all yellow.
  • In Generation 4 coverage you can also get a plate with a large orange circle in the middle.
  • Front plates are required in Alaska.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Tall Snow Mountains
metas.note: • On a lot of the Alaskan coverage you will be able to see tall, snow covered mountains.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Alaska - Thin Trees
metas.note: • Trees in Alaska are generally thinner and have less broad leaves than those seen in the other 49 states.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Bold Font Signs
metas.note:
• The numbers on speed signs are written in a bold font.

--- NOTE:

  • The font is much thinner on speed signs in Montenegro.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Bollards
metas.note:
• Albanian bollards have a black top with a red and grey reflector.
  • The bottom is painted white.

--- NOTE:

  • Italy uses the same kind of bollards.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Albanian chevrons are white on black.

--- NOTE:

  • Within southern Europe this chevron is also used by Italy, Greece, and Spain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Guardrail Endings
metas.note:
• These flat and wide guardrail endings that bend away from the road can often be found in Albania.

--- NOTE:

  • The same endings are found in Italy.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Horizontal Bar Poles
metas.note:
• Other, more simple Albanian pole tops will often have horizontal bars.

--- NOTE:

  • If you are not sure between Montenegro or Albania and see these poles, guess Albania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - License Plates
metas.note:
• Albanian licence plates either have blue strips on both sides or a single red strip on the left side.

--- NOTE:

  • Albania is the only European country with red on the left side of the licence plate.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Rifts
metas.note:
• Rifts can commonly be seen in Albanian coverage, due to poor stitching.

--- NOTE:

  • Rifts are also equally common in Montenegro, and can rarely be seen in various other countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - RRUGA
metas.note: • The Albanian word for street is rruga.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Upside Down Poles
metas.note:
• These pole tops, with an upside down triangle shape, are a good clue for Albania.

--- NOTE:

  • Serbia, Czechia, Slovakia and Romania use similar pole tops.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Albania - Water Tanks
metas.note:
• You will see a lot of cylinder-shaped water tanks on the roofs of buildings.

--- NOTE:

  • This is less common in Montenegro.
  • Some parts of Turkey also have a lot of similar-looking water tanks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: American Samoa - Unique Car
metas.note: • A slightly rusted black truck bed can be seen on the main island of Tutuila.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Andorra - Architecture
metas.note:
• Andorra has a lot of these stone buildings.
  • They can be seen almost everywhere in the country.

--- NOTE:

  • These buildings can also be found close to Andorra, in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/andorra for more clues.

metas.name: Andorra - Gen 3 Autumn
metas.note: • All the Generation 3 coverage was taken in October, meaning that many deciduous trees have autumn colours.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/andorra for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Black Car
metas.note:
• Argentina has a black Google car in Generation 3 coverage.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South America, only Argentina, Peru and Uruguay have a black Google car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Argentina typically uses white-and-red chevrons.

--- NOTE:

  • Argentina is the only American country with these chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
• Argentinian kilometre markers are typically white with a black strip displaying the road number at the top.

--- NOTE:

  • The markers on national highways are indicated with RN, while RP indicates a provincial highway.
  • National highways will be labelled white on the map, while provincial highways will be labelled green.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - License Plates
metas.note:
Argentina uses two types of licence plates:

  • A black one, which will be visible on street view with a black dot in the middle.
  • A white one with a blue bar at the top.

--- NOTE:

  • The black dot can only be found on Argentinian licence plates, while the blue bar can be found in Brazil as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Poles
metas.note:
• Round concrete poles sustaining three electricity lines in an alternating pattern are very common in Argentina.
  • Doubled up poles are also a good clue for Argentina.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar doubled concrete poles can occasionally be found throughout Bolivia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Roadlines
metas.note: • Road lines in Argentina are mainly dashed white, double yellow or a mix in between.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Black Give-Way Sign
metas.note:
• Give-way signs in Australia have a white border and black text.

--- NOTE:

  • New Zealand’s give-way signs use red, instead of black, text.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Australian bollards are white, with a red reflector on the front, and a grey reflector on the back.

--- NOTE:

  • New Zealand uses a bollard where the red reflector wraps around the back, meaning the reflector goes from end to end while the Australian one stops in the middle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Eucalyptus Trees
metas.note:
• Eucalyptus trees are by far the most common type of tree in Australia.
  • Their bark is typically light-coloured, with puffy puffy clusters of leaves.

--- NOTE:

  • Their look may vary significantly, depending on your location within the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Australia uses almost exclusively white road lines.

--- NOTE:

  • New Zealand can have all white road lines as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Austria - Architecture
metas.note:
• Alpine architecture is common in Austria and other countries in the Alps.
  • Houses commonly have distinct light coloured walls, with wooden elements such as balconies or panelling around the top floor, with dark-coloured wooden roofs that extend outward.

--- NOTE:

  • Germany uses similar architecture in its southern states.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/austria for more clues.

metas.name: Austria - Bollards
metas.note:
• Austria uses white bollards, with a black top.
  • The colour of the reflector is (dark) red or dark grey.
  • Many bollards also feature a small nipple-shaped black cap on the top.

--- NOTE:

  • Slovenia and Montenegro use the same bollards, but with bright red reflectors instead of grey or dark red.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/austria for more clues.

metas.name: Austria - Chevrons
metas.note:
Austria uses two colour schemes for chevrons:

  • White on red
  • Red on yellow

--- NOTE:

  • Germany mostly uses red on white chevrons, and rarely red on yellow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/austria for more clues.

metas.name: Austria - Einbahn
metas.note:
• These one-way traffic signs, with the word ‘EINBAHN’ written on them, are unique to Austria.

--- NOTE:

  • In Germany there will be “Einbahnstraße” written on the sign.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/austria for more clues.

metas.name: Austria - Landscape
metas.note:
• Most of Austria is mountainous and covered in forests.
  • However, some areas in the east and northeast are much more flat and agricultural.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/austria for more clues.

metas.name: Azores - Dry Rock Walls
metas.note:
• Dry rock walls made of volcanic rocks are very common on the Azores.

--- NOTE:

  • Dry rock walls are not common on Madeira, and while they are somewhat common on mainland Portugal, they will not be made of volcanic rocks.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Azores - Hydrangeas
metas.note:
• Hydrangeas can commonly be seen on the Azores.

--- NOTE:

  • They can rarely be found on Madeira.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Azores - Landscape
metas.note:
• Most of the Azores visible on Street View consists of open agricultural fields in a rolling landscape, often with taller round hills in the background.

--- NOTE:

  • Madeira has a very mountainous landscape, and very rarely has open agricultural fields.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Agricultural Fields & Water
metas.note: • Bodies of water and agricultural fields can be often seen beside the streets of Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
- In Generation 3 coverage, these three cars can be seen in Bangladesh:

  • The red mirror with bars, classic white and striped white car.

--- NOTE:

  • The classic white car is the only car that is not unique to Bangladesh.
  • Make sure to not mix up the striped white with the Cambodian car, since they look similar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Gen 4 Cars
metas.note:
- In Generation 4 coverage, two Street View cars can be seen in Bangladesh:

  • A black car and a white car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Rickshaws
metas.note:
• Rickshaws are frequently found all around Bangladesh, especially the green auto rickshaws.

--- NOTE:

  • They are found in other Asian countries as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Bangladesh, as well as a variety of other countries, has received some poor quality coverage, also known as “Shitcam”.
  • The Shitcam car colours are black and white.

--- NOTE:

  • Sometimes the car colour can be fully obstructed by a big circular blur.

--- TIP:

  • Shitcam is only found around Dhaka.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Bangladesh often have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan, India and Malaysia.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bangladesh for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Additional Blue Signs
metas.note:
• Road signs often have an additional small blue sign.
  • In other European countries, these small signs are usually just white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Bollards
metas.note:
• Belgium uses white bollards with a yellow rectangular reflector on the front and white on the back.
  • A second type of bollard is dark brown with two red stripes at the top.

--- NOTE:

  • Denmark uses similar white bollards, but they have a red stripe at the top and the reflector is not rectangular.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Concrete Roads
metas.note:
• A lot of rural roads in Belgium are made out of concrete slabs, almost like you would see in the Philippines or Thailand.

--- NOTE:

  • The Netherlands almost never uses concrete slabs for roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Double Gutters
metas.note:
• Almost all roads (big or small) in Belgium use gutters on both sides.
  • This is much less common in neighbouring countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Red License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Belgium use red text.
  • You can recognise this distinct colour even through the blur.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Small Priority Signs
metas.note: • Priority signs in Belgium have an orange diamond and are much smaller than in other countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Square Poles
metas.note:
• Most poles in Belgium are concrete, square shaped, and have tiny holes running up them.
  • They often have small metal wrappings around them.
  • The second most common type of pole has oval-shaped holes.

--- NOTE:

  • The small metal wrappings can be found in France as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Yellow Reflectors
metas.note:
• Belgium uses A-type guardrails with yellow reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • In Europe, only Spain, Andorra, and Belgium use these reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Bermuda - Unique Car
metas.note: • Bermuda features a black Street View car with the entire front sides of the vehicle typically visible.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Architecture
metas.note:
• The traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct.
  • Most of the houses have tin roofs and wooden painted frames, which give them a unique look.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Car
metas.note:
• Coverage in Bhutan was taken by a grey Google car without an antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • Bhutan is the only left hand driving country which has a grey Google car.
  • Make sure to not mix it up with a white Google car, since they can look similar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Landscape
metas.note:
• Bhutan is a mountainous country and most of the coverage is located on its main mountain roads.

--- NOTE:

  • In the south are flat areas where you cannot see any mountains.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Bhutan are almost always red and can easily be seen on vehicles.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, Bhutan is the only country that uses full red licence plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Painted Poles
metas.note:
• Thin metal poles are occasionally found in Bhutan.
  • They are often painted black at the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Stone Blocks
metas.note:
• Bhutan commonly uses these stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads.
  • These blocks are very common and often one of the best ways to recognize rural Bhutan rounds.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Architecture
metas.note:
• Many buildings in Bolivia consist of large red bricks.
  • Buildings often have an ‘unfinished' look.

--- NOTE:

  • This style of architecture is also common in parts of Peru.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Cobblestone Roads
metas.note:
• There are also a lot of cobblestone roads.
  • These roads often have a specific pattern, with several neat lines of stones separating the more disorganised cobblestones in between.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Concrete Roads
metas.note: • Bolivia has a lot of standard asphalt roads, but concrete slab roads are also fairly common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Curvy Poles
metas.note:
• Many wooden utility poles, particularly in the eastern parts of Bolivia’s Street View coverage, are noticeably curvy and look like they are made from locally sourced tree trunks.

--- NOTE:

  • While you may see slightly bent poles in other places, extremely curvy poles are a very good clue for Bolivia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Red Rocks
metas.note:
• If you have a tough 50-50, it can help to look at the colour of the rocks and soil, which often have a distinct reddish tint in Bolivia, more so than the other Andean countries.

--- NOTE:

  • This information should be used with a fair amount of caution, as there are many variables.
  • Only use it when you have no other clues available.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - White Car
metas.note:
• Bolivia only has Generation 3 camera coverage.
  • All of the country was covered by a white Google car with no antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • In Latin America, white cars with no antenna can also be found in Peru and Chile.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - A Roads
metas.note:
• Just like the other Southern African countries, direction signs have a green background.
  • The numbers of major roads start with A.
  • These road numbers frequently appear on direction signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Road numbers in South Africa never start with A.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Chevrons
metas.note:
• These small red-and-white chevrons can sometimes be found next to the road.

--- NOTE:

  • They are also very common in South Africa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Landscape
metas.note:
• The typical Botswana landscape is dry and mostly flat, though a limited amount of elevation can be found in certain regions.
  • Common vegetation includes shrubs, small trees, and occasionally dry, golden grasslands.
  • The soil is arid, sandy and ranges in colour from white to red.

--- NOTE:

  • The border region of South Africa can have a similar landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - License Plates
metas.note:
• Botswana has white front plates and yellow rear plates, similar to UK-style plates.

--- NOTE:

  • Botswana is the only country in southern Africa where yellow rear plates are predominantly found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Old Road Signs
metas.note:
• Some road signs have a blue background.
  • This is an older style of sign that was used before signs with white backgrounds were introduced.
  • They are relatively unique to Botswana.

--- NOTE:

  • Most road signs will have the newer white background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Like the other countries in Southern Africa, outside road lines (if present) are yellow, while centre road lines are white.

--- NOTE:

  • Outside yellow road lines in arid environments also exist in Israel, Palestine, Jordan, and the UAE.
  • However, these countries all drive on the right side.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Striped Curbs & Guardrails
metas.note:
• Curbs and guardrails are usually striped.
  • Possible colour schemes are black-and-yellow, red-and-white, and black-and-white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Botswana has a unique black-and-yellow striped signpost.
  • More rarely, you can see red-and-white signposts.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southern Africa, these signposts are only found in Botswana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - White Car
metas.note:
• All of Botswana was covered by a white Google car without an antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Africa, this car can also be found in South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Black Signs
metas.note: • Most Brazilian road signs have the backs painted black.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Blue Road Markers
metas.note: • Blue road markers with the road number and kilometre can be seen on the sides of roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Blue Water Tanks
metas.note: • Blue Fortlev water tanks are often seen on Brazilian roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Chevrons
metas.note: • Brazil uses yellow on black chevrons, as opposed to most of South America, which use black on yellow chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Curbs
metas.note: • There are frequently white painted kerbs on Brazilian roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Brazil were white until 2018.
  • Now, a white plate with a blue stripe on top is used.
  • Red is still used for commercial vehicles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Orange Tiled Roofs
metas.note: • Many houses throughout Brazil have orange tiled roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Poles
metas.note:
• The most common poles in Brazil have some resemblance to a ladder in the bottom portion.
  • They are rectangular, have long segments running through the bottom, and small holes near the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Red Soil
metas.note:
• Soil in most of Brazil is distinctly red.
  • It can range from a light pink around Mato Grosso to a deep maroon near the Paraná river.
  • The soil is usually not red in the North East, or in the majority of Rio Grande do Sul, however.

--- NOTE:

  • The nearby Argentine province of Misiones has deep red soil, as well a handful of other countries and regions around the world.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Satellite Dishes
metas.note: • It is fairly common to see transparent satellite dishes, which within Latin America is generally unique to Brazil.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Alternating Poles
metas.note:
• This style of pole top, with 3 large, alternating insulators that are shaped like upward facing hooks, is a good clue for Bulgaria.
  • This pole top is probably unique to the country.

--- NOTE:

  • You can also find this pole top with the insulators facing downwards.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Gen 3 Winter
metas.note:
• The majority of Generation 3 coverage in Bulgaria was taken during March and April, resulting in very distinct dead-looking “winter” coverage.

--- NOTE:

  • Hungary and Czechia also have a lot of similar dead-looking Generation 3 coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Grey Tape
metas.note:
• You can commonly see a small piece of grey tape at the top of the car antenna in Generation 3 coverage.
  • Not all Gen 3 coverage has this tape.

--- NOTE:

  • This can also be seen in Czechia, Slovakia, Hungary, and Romania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Hook Poles
metas.note: • Most poles have small, alternating hook-shaped insulators.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Thin Roadlines
metas.note:
• Bulgaria usually has thin roadlines.
  • This is particularly useful to tell Bulgaria apart from Romania, where roadlines are usually much thicker.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Town Entry Signs
metas.note:
• Town entry signs have a simple white design and also use both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabet.
  • Like with the directional signs, the two lines of text are obvious, even when seen from far away.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Bollards
metas.note:
Cambodia has a variety of different bollards. The most common ones are:

  • A stone bollard with red-and-white stripes.
  • A stone bollard with a red top and a white base, usually with a reflector in the red part.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
--- GENERATION 3 CARS:

  • A car with a short, stubby antenna.
  • The antenna has three ridges.

➖➖➖➖➖

  • A white car with stripes and no antenna.
  • There is a white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right.

--- NOTE:

  • This specific striped white car is unique to Cambodia.
  • Make sure not to mix it up with the Bangladeshi striped car, which looks slightly different.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Houses On Stilts
metas.note:
• Wooden houses on stilts are common.
  • Walls are often made of vertical planks.
  • Many homes have double or triple roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Poles
metas.note:
Two types of poles are common:

  • Concrete ladder poles (so named because the indents and ridges resemble a ladder).
  • Round concrete poles with small holes.
  • Rarely, you might see simple wooden poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads have dashed or solid yellow middle road lines.
  • Outer road lines are somewhat rare, but when present, they are solid white.

--- NOTE:

  • Thailand uses similar road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Cambodia.
  • This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
  • It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, India, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka also have shitcam coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Diamond Sign
metas.note:
• Canada uses unique diamond-shaped T-Intersection signs.
  • Some provinces use different designs.

--- NOTE:

  • Canada is the only country in the world where you can find these signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Gen 2
metas.note:
• Canada has a fair amount of Generation 2 coverage, especially in rural or remote areas.
  • Generation 2 can be recognized by the big circular car blur and the halo-like colour distortion in the sky.

--- NOTE:

  • If you are between Canada and the US, and the location is in Generation 2, you are much more likely to be in Canada.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Maximum Speed Sign
metas.note:
• Canada uses the word ‘maximum’ on speed signs.

--- NOTE:

  • The US uses the words ‘speed limit’ on such signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec Arret
metas.note: • Stop signs with the word ‘Arrêt’ are unique to Québec.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Canadian roads usually have single yellow centre lines.
  • However, double middle yellow centre lines are still decently common.

--- NOTE:

  • Double yellow centre lines are more common in the US.
  • This is not a 100% reliable clue, so make sure to use this along with other clues.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Poles
metas.note:
• Chile uses square concrete poles with an indent on both sides.
  • They are somewhat similar to Brazilian poles, however have fewer horizontal supports in the indent.
  • The upper part typically has small pinholes.
  • Wooden poles are also fairly common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/chile for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Chilean road lines are either all white or all yellow.
  • You will almost never see a combination of the two colours, apart from a few rare exceptions.

--- NOTE:

  • It is important to note that Argentina has a decent amount of roads with all white road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/chile for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Signpost Slots
metas.note: • Slots can often be seen at the top of signposts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/chile for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Unique Car
metas.note:
• Chile has a white Google Car with no antenna in Generation 3.
  • There are two variants
  • A blue Google Car can be seen in Generation 4.

--- NOTE:

  • In Generation 3, a plain white Google Car with no antenna can also be seen in Peru and Bolivia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/chile for more clues.

metas.name: Christmas Island - Unique Car
metas.note:
The car coverage was done with a unique Google car:

  • A silver pickup truck, with the bed of the truck visible.
  • Usually, this is all you need to identify Christmas Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/christmas-island for more clues.

metas.name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands - Unique Car
metas.note: • This unique car with a snorkel at the front right and the edges of the bed visible is found on West Island.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Black & Yellow Sticker
metas.note: • Colombian poles are often marked with unique black-and-yellow or black-and-orange stripes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Cross
metas.note:
• Signposts in Colombia are made of white metal, and join to form a distinct cross on the back of signs.

--- NOTE:

  • White metal signposts can also be found in Brazil, however these are usually wider.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - License Plates
metas.note:
• Colombian licence plates are typically yellow.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South America, yellow licence plates are almost exclusively found in Colombia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Stubby Antenna
metas.note:
• In Generation 3 coverage, a short thick antenna is sometimes visible with a black, white or grey car.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Americas, you can also find the antenna in Mexico, Ecuador and Brazil.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Wooden Fences
metas.note:
• Wooden fences are particularly common in Colombia.

--- NOTE:

  • In addition to the unpainted variants, some fence posts are painted and sharp at the top.
  • These are almost exclusive to Colombia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - B-Type Guardrails
metas.note:
• Croatia has square (B-type) guardrails.

--- NOTE:

  • Croatia is one of the few European countries that use B-type guardrails.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Blue Fire Hydrants
metas.note:
• Croatia features blue fire hydrants with two diagonal protrusions on either side.
  • Newer fire hydrants seen in Generation 4 have a smaller top but are still recognisable due to the blue paint.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar fire hydrants can be found in bordering countries, most commonly in Hungary.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Croatian bollards are white with a black rectangle and red or white reflector.
  • From the top, it is shaped like a triangle.

--- NOTE:

  • Hungarian and Lithuanian bollards look similar, but have more rounded edges compared to Croatia’s sharper edges.
  • Lithuanian bollards will also have an orange reflector.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Gen 3 Mirror
metas.note:
• Generation 3 coverage often has a non-standard car blur where the side mirrors of the car are partially visible.
  • This is not unique to Croatia, but by far most common there.

--- NOTE:

  • Sometimes, you can see a small circular yellow sticker on the car mirror.
  • This sticker is unique to Croatia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Red Brick Architecture
metas.note:
• Buildings in Croatia sometimes feature exposed red brick walls.
  • This architecture is more common in inland areas.

--- NOTE:

  • This type of architecture can also be found in Slovenia and Serbia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Curaçao - Unique Car
metas.note: • This black car with a roof rack is unique to Curaçao.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Black Caps
metas.note:
• Czech sign posts typically have thick, black caps.

--- NOTE:

  • While some European countries have similar caps, Slovakia usually does not have them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Bollards in Czechia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back.
  • There are also rarer blue and red variants.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other country with the same design is Slovakia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Direction Signs
metas.note:
• Czechia uses arrow-shaped directional signs with a filled in tip.
  • Due to the shape, they are recognizable from behind.

--- NOTE:

  • Slovakia has small white arrows instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - House Numbers
metas.note:
• House numbers in Czechia are generally written on blue or red signs with thin white borders.

--- NOTE:

  • On the contrary, Slovak house numbers are typically written on white signs with a thin red or black border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - No Center Lines
metas.note:
• Czechia often has solid outer roadlines, with no centre line.

--- NOTE:

  • While these roadlines can be found in all neighbouring countries, it is notably also common in Germany.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Pair Houses
metas.note:
• Suburban houses in Czechia are commonly connected in pairs.

--- NOTE:

  • This is less common in most neighbouring countries, including Slovakia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Pair Poles
metas.note: • Czechia and Slovakia most commonly use wide, round concrete poles, which are quite often attached in pairs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Railway Crossing
metas.note:
• Czech railway crossing signs do not have a background.

--- NOTE:

  • Slovak railway crossing signs have a white rectangular background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Rolling Landscape
metas.note:
• The Czech landscape is fairly rolling, with a lot of hills and altitude changes, but not a lot of tall mountains.
  • Generally speaking, Slovakia has more mountains, but also more completely flat areas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Special B-Type Guardrails
metas.note:
• Czechia and Slovakia both use a special kind of type B guardrail, which is wider than the normal type.
  • No other European countries use the same kind.

--- NOTE:

  • While Slovakia occasionally uses other types of guardrails, Czechia is fairly consistent.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Thin Font Road Signs
metas.note:
• Czech road signs have a fairly thin font.

--- NOTE:

  • Slovak signs normally have a much bolder font.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Bollards
metas.note:
• Denmark has a very recognizable white bollard with a yellow reflector and a dark orange stripe.
  • This bollard is unique to the country.

--- NOTE:

  • Belgium has bollards that may look somewhat similar.
  • However, it will never feature the orange stripe.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Direction Signs
metas.note:
• Denmark has very unique-looking direction signs that are very useful to recognize the country.
  • They are low to the ground and framed by pipes.
  • They are either coloured red and white or blue and white, with a directional arrow incorporated into the background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Double "Splitted" Roadlines
metas.note:
• Denmark has all-white road lines.
  • Double middle lines are very common.

--- NOTE:

  • Some other European countries, most notably Poland and Greece, can have double middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Landscape
metas.note:
• Denmark is a generally flat country with wide, open fields between towns.
  • Suburban areas are usually open, with space between buildings.
  • Urban cores are more dense and built up.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Pipe Signs
metas.note: • This signpost, where the pipe frame is bent around the sign, is unique to Denmark.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Square Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer road lines often consist of small white squares.
  • These unique-looking lines are a good way to identify Denmark.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Town Signs
metas.note:
• This unique sign is found when entering a town.
  • When leaving, there will be a red slash through the sign.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Vej
metas.note:
• Most Danish street names end in “vej.”
  • This is the Danish word for “street.”
  • Street signs most commonly have a blue background with white text.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Dominican Republic - Unique Car
metas.note:
• This unique car was used for all street view coverage in the Dominican Republic.
  • It can be recognized by the two metal bars, the thick black stripes on them, as well as the white hood visible at the front.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Architecture
metas.note:
• Most houses are made of grey bricks and have metal roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • This is not unique to Ecuador, but is very common.
  • Countries such as Peru, and especially Bolivia, commonly use red bricks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Bollards
metas.note:
You will find two main types of bollards:

  • A round bollard with two red stripes,
  • A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black.

--- NOTE:

  • Many other bollards can be found, however, they will almost always have the same colour scheme and style.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Chevron Spam
metas.note:
• Ecuador often uses a lot of chevrons in road curves (“chevron spam”), usually considerably more than most other Latin American countries.

--- NOTE:

  • Colombia also occasionally uses a lot of chevrons in curves.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Double Guardrails
metas.note:
• Double guardrails are very commonly used.
  • This is much less common in other South American countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• All Generation 4 coverage was captured using a white pickup truck with a black trunk and no antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • The pickup truck in Panama has an antenna on the front.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Ladder Poles
metas.note:
• Most poles in Ecuador are round and made of concrete.
  • These poles are fairly generic and not all that useful to identify the country.

However, sometimes you will see another, more useful type of concrete pole: The ladder pole.

  • It has a lot of small indents – resembling the steps of a ladder.
  • Within Latin America, these poles are more or less unique to Ecuador.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - License Plates
metas.note:
• The standard licence plates are white and can be short or long.
  • In street view, you will often see a mix of both sizes.
  • Commercial vehicles, such as taxis or buses, can have older solid orange plates, or newer ones with an orange bar at the top.

--- NOTE:

  • Ecuador is the only country in Latin America to use a mix of short and long licence plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Ecuador.
  • This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
  • It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Latin America, Ecuador is the only country that has shitcam coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Square Road Signs
metas.note: • Ecuador uses a lot of square road signs with a white background, of the design shown in the image.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Stubby Antenna
metas.note:
• All Generation 3 coverage is made with a white car, with a short and thick antenna (“stubby antenna”).
  • The antenna and or car are not always visible.

--- NOTE:

  • Mexico, Brazil and Colombia can also have this same short antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Estonian bollards have a round, baton-like shape.
  • They have a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back.
  • The reflectors can be white or orange.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Estonia uses red chevrons with white arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Russia and Ukraine use the same chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Dashed Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer road lines sometimes consist of short dashes.

--- NOTE:

  • Lithuania also sometimes has short dashes.
  • In addition, Sweden primarily uses short dashes as outer road lines.
  • Sweden's dashes are closer to the edge of the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.

  • However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
  • In Estonia, the marker will be perpendicular to the road.
  • It has numbers on both sides of the marker.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Metal Cap
metas.note:
• Most wooden poles have a small metal cap on top, similar to those found in the Nordic countries.

--- NOTE:

  • Alongside the Nordic countries of Sweden, Finland and Norway, these caps can also sometimes be found in Latvia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - No Border Signs
metas.note:
• Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
  • Estonian signs have a thin red border, with no white outline around it.
  • The red border extends all the way to the edge of the sign.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - No Reflectors
metas.note:
• Estonia has normal A-type guardrails with no reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • The other two Baltic countries can have reflectors on their guardrails.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Square Poles
metas.note:
• You can additionally find a fair amount of square concrete poles, often also with diagonal supports.
  • These are similar to those found in Lithuania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Tee & Tn
metas.note:
• The Estonian words for street and road are tänav and tee, respectively.
  • These words are unique to Estonian.
  • Tänav is often abbreviated as ‘tn’.

--- NOTE:

  • The Finnish suffix -tie, meaning street, can look similar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Trident Poles
metas.note:
Trident pole tops are somewhat common:

  • This pole top features one insulator on top, and two to the side.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Concrete Bus Shelters
metas.note: • Concrete bus shelters are a common sight on roads in Eswatini.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Landscape
metas.note:
• Eswatini’s landscape is known for its green, wooded hills and tall golden grass.

--- NOTE:

  • In contrast, Lesotho’s mountains are typically barren, and long grass is not a common sight there.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Eswatini are long and green at the bottom.

--- NOTE:

  • These may look similar to certain South African plates.
  • Make sure to refer to other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - MR Roads
metas.note: • Roads starting with the letters “MR” are exclusive to Eswatini.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Poles
metas.note:
• Poles in Eswatini are made of dark brown wood and follow a simple design.
  • The insulators are mostly mounted on the side.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southern Africa, three insulators on the pole are more commonly found in Eswatini.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Eswatini typically uses yellow outside lines and occasionally, triple white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar road lines can also be found in South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Eswatini - White Car
metas.note:
• All of Eswatini was covered by a white Google car without an antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Africa, this car can also be found in South Africa, Lesotho and Botswana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/eswatini for more clues.

metas.name: Faroe Islands - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• The generation 4 coverage was captured with a black pickup truck with an antenna on the front.
  • The truck is always blurred.

--- NOTE:

  • The truck in Iceland does not have a similar antenna.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Faroe Islands - Landscape
metas.note:
• The landscape of the Faroe islands is characterised by long, wide fjords with jagged green mountains that rise straight out of the water, with rocky ridge lines along the mountainsides.
  • The mountains generally look more imposing and greener than coastal mountains in Iceland, which can often be used to tell them apart.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Architecture
metas.note:
• Finnish architecture is mostly modern and utilitarian.
  • Downtown areas tend to be very modern, with lots of apartment buildings and use of concrete.
  • Suburbs mostly consist of freestanding single family homes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Bollards
metas.note:
• Finland has long black-and-white bollards with a rectangular, white reflector on the front and two dots on the back.
  • They can be either round or thin and curved.
  • The black strip is typically diagonal.

--- NOTE:

  • They can look somewhat similar to bollards found in other Northern European countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Direction Signs
metas.note: • Finnish directional signs consist of a solid blue background, white text, and a white border with guiding arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Full Roadlines
metas.note:
• Where present, outer road lines will always be solid white lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Unlike Sweden and Norway, Finland does not use dashed outside lines.
  • The only exception to this are the Åland Islands in southwest Finland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Gen 3 Autumn
metas.note:
• A lot of Generation 3 coverage was taken in autumn, meaning that trees in this coverage often have distinct fall colours.

--- NOTE:

  • This is significantly less common in Generation 3 coverage in the other Nordics.
  • This means that when you are faced with a tough decision between countries, a fall vibe can be a good clue for Finland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Finland.
  • This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
  • It has a wide circular car blur, and can be distinguished from Generation 2 by its lack of a sky halo and often somewhat brownish colours.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Europe, Finland is the only country that has coverage with this camera.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Snow Poles
metas.note:
• In Finland, it is common to find orange snow poles with a thin white band near the top.

--- NOTE:

  • These are also found commonly in Norway and Sweden, but with a much wider white band, lower down on the pole.
  • They can also have multiple white bands, while Finnish snow poles usually have just one band.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Tie & Katu
metas.note:
• Most Finnish street names end in “tie” or “katu.”
  • These are the Finnish words for road and street.

--- NOTE:

  • You may find roads ending in “polku” and “kuja”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Yellow Road Signs
metas.note:
• Finnish road signs have a yellow background.

--- NOTE:

  • Signs in Sweden and Iceland also have yellow backgrounds.
  • Norway, however, has signs with a white background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: Finland - Yellow Sign Border
metas.note:
• On traffic signs that have a red border, you will find a thin yellow stroke on the edge of the sign.

--- NOTE:

  • You will not see this in any other Nordic country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/finland for more clues.

metas.name: France - Blue Sticker
metas.note:
• Small blue rectangular markings on utility poles are unique to France.
  • They are often referred to as ‘stickers’ by the community, but are actually small plates.

--- NOTE:

  • You will find these plates on almost all wooden and metallic poles, but not as often on ladder poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Bollards
metas.note:
• The French bollard is extremely recognizable and appears very often.
  • It is a round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band going all the way around.
  • The band can be grey or red.
  • Some rare variations have a fully red top.

--- NOTE:

  • A bollard that is commonly found in Scotland looks similar, but has a blunt top instead of a pointed one.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Chevrons
metas.note:
• France uses chevrons with white arrows on a blue background.
  • They can have a wide amount of arrows, ranging from one to five.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other European country with this colour scheme is Spain, where you will only find chevrons with two or four arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - French Pole Tops
metas.note:
• Diamond shaped pole tops with three wires are commonly called “French poletops” within the community.
  • They are most frequently found on top of ladder poles.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Europe, “French poletops” in conjunction with ladder poles are also common in Spain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Ladder Poles
metas.note:
• Concrete poles with step-like indents are common in France.
  • They are referred to as ladder or waffle poles by the community.

--- NOTE:

  • They are also common in Spain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - License Plates
metas.note:
• Modern French plates are long and white, with blue strips on both sides of the plate.
  • The left strip will be more visible than the right strip.

--- NOTE:

  • Some older French plates lack the right blue strip, with the rear plate being yellow.
  • These are very rare in newer coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Long Dashed Outlines
metas.note: • Typical French roads have long spaced out dashes on the outside.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Long Middle Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle lines with dashes that are longer than usual can be a good clue for France.

--- NOTE:

  • Unusually long dashes are also common in the UK.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Offset Block Roadlines
metas.note:
• These middle road lines, where each dash consists of two offset blocks, are unique to France.
  • They are not extremely common, but when you see them, you can safely guess France.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Rectangular Signposts
metas.note:
• Many traffic signs in France have flat rectangular signposts.
  • Signposts, along with signbacks, can be dyed with unorthodox colours, more so than in other countries.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other European countries with flat signposts are Portugal, Spain, and Andorra.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Rue
metas.note: • The French word for street is “rue”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Short Signposts
metas.note: • Traffic signs with particularly short signposts are very common in France.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - White Border Road Signs
metas.note:
• French road signs have a red border with a thin white outline.
  • You will often find white rectangular signs with black text below traffic signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Road signs in Spain have a thick red border that goes all the way to the edge.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Bollards
metas.note:
• Germany uses these black and white bollards, with white and light-grey reflectors.
  • The reflector will be orange on bollards next to intersections.
  • Many bollards also feature blue attachments on the side.

--- NOTE:

  • Luxembourg uses almost identical bollards, but they have 3 bolts instead of 2 on the reflector.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Einbahnstraße
metas.note:
• These one-way traffic signs, with the word ‘Einbahnstraße’ written on them, are unique to Germany.

--- NOTE:

  • In Austria, there will be “EINBAHN” written on the sign.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Gen 4
metas.note: • All car coverage in Germany is made with a Generation 4 camera.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - No Stopping Signs
metas.note: • “No Stopping” and “No Waiting” signs in Germany will often have white arrows drawn on them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Pole Tops
metas.note:
The most common pole tops are:

  • A horizontal bar with uneven hanging insulators.
  • A Triangle pole top.
  • All kinds of T-Shaped pole tops, which can have varying insulator setups.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Sign Back Sticker
metas.note:
• You can commonly find black or dark grey sign backs, which are rather rare in Europe.
  • Most signs will also feature this sticker, with an upside-down red triangle on a black rectangle.

--- NOTE:

  • Italy, Romania and Albania also have black sign backs, however landscape should be sufficient to tell them apart.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Town Entry Signs
metas.note:
• German town entry signs are yellow with black text and have a metallic frame.

--- NOTE:

These signs can include a lot of useful information too:

  • The town and or city name on the top.
  • The Municipality in the middle.
  • And the county on the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - White Sticker Poles
metas.note: • Most wooden poles in Germany will feature a rectangular white sticker.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Multicolored Body Parts
metas.note:
• Taxis in Ghana typically have multicoloured body panels.
  • The fenders and quarter panels are always coloured orange-yellow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Poles
metas.note: • Ghana typically uses wooden poles with 3 insulators on a metallic crossbar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Road lines in Ghana are always white.
  • However, many paved roads do not have road lines at all.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Black and white striped signposts in Ghana are typically seen in cities.
  • On rural roads, you will mostly see classic, non-painted, metal signposts.

--- NOTE:

  • Black and white signposts can be seen in other countries as well.
  • Make sure to look at other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Ghana - Unique Car
metas.note:
• All regular road coverage in Ghana was made with a unique Google car.
  • It has a visible roof rack with a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar.
  • In addition, the hood of the car is usually visible, showing a street view car wrapping that features a red rectangle and some other recognizable elements.
  • Normally, this unique car is all you need to identify Ghana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Gibraltar - White Tip Antenna
metas.note:
• All coverage in Gibraltar is Generation 3.
  • The car will always have a unique long antenna with a silver tip, often referred to simply as the “Gibraltar antenna” by the community.

--- NOTE:

  • This antenna can also be found in parts of Spain, but nowhere else in Europe.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Gibraltar - Yellow License Plates
metas.note:
• Like the UK, Gibraltar uses yellow back plates on vehicles.
  • However, note that unlike the UK, Gibraltar drives on the right.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Bollards
metas.note: • Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with almost square reflectors, being red on the front and white on the back.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Greek chevrons have white arrows on a black background.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar chevrons are found in Albania, Italy and the UK.
  • Spain has the same colours, but will almost always have either two or four arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Dark Wooden Poles
metas.note:
• Greek utility poles are primarily wooden, and often have a distinctly dark brown colour.
  • They will often be noticeably taller than in other countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Double Faded Roadlines
metas.note:
• In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines.
  • This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Gen 3 Winter
metas.note: • Greece has a lot of Generation 3 winter and fall coverage, which tends to look somewhat bleak and depressing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Harp Poles
metas.note: • These distinctive poletops, which have a metal frame shaped vaguely like a harp, are unique to Greece.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Small Lamp
metas.note:
• This type of small lamp, attached to the side of poles with a round shade above the light bulb.

--- NOTE:

  • You can also find them in North Macedonia and Serbia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Warning Signs
metas.note: • Greek warning signs have a red border and a yellow background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Yellow Roadlines
metas.note: • Yellow road lines are more common in Greece than any other southern European country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greenland - Architecture
metas.note:
• Greenlandic architecture mainly consists of small, colourful, simple looking wooden houses, which even in cities are typically placed quite sparsely.
  • The major cities have some larger buildings, which normally look fairly minimalistic.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Greenland - Odd Google Cars
metas.note: • Most locations with coverage will have their own odd and unique Street View vehicles, ranging from a red tractor to a snowmobile with a large box at the front.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Guam - Car
metas.note:
• The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right and a tiny part of the roof rack can be seen.

--- NOTE:

  • You will not see a roof rack on the Northern Mariana Islands Google car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guam for more clues.

metas.name: Guam - Poles
metas.note:
• Poles on Guam are almost always concrete and commonly very thick.

--- NOTE:

  • Northern Mariana Islands typically have wooden poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guam for more clues.

metas.name: Guam - Road Reflectors
metas.note: • Both Guam and Northern Mariana Islands often have a very large number of road reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guam for more clues.

metas.name: Guatemala - Painted Poles
metas.note: • In Guatemala you will very commonly see poles painted with either pink, green or a combination of the two.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guatemala for more clues.

metas.name: Guatemala - Unique Car
metas.note:
• This grey Street View car with a visible roof rack and side mirrors can be seen on all car coverage in Guatemala.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other tropical country with a similar car is Laos.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guatemala for more clues.

metas.name: Hawaii - License Plates
metas.note:
• The most common Hawaii licence plate is white with an arcing rainbow across the centre of the plate.
  • When blurred, you can sometimes see the outline of the rainbow.
  • Front plates are required in Hawaii.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hawaii - Own Language
metas.note:
• Hawaii is the only state to use its own language, though English is still predominantly used.
  • Most place names are in Hawaiian, so you can spot it on street signs, and other road markers.

--- NOTE:

  • Every Hawaiian word ends in one of 5 vowels: A, E, I, O, or U.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hawaii - Pavement Markers
metas.note:
Raised pavement markers in Hawaii will commonly be placed in a specific pattern:

  • A single reflector, followed by four reflectors put close together and then a single reflector, repeating the pattern.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Air Conditioners
metas.note: • Because of the subtropical climate, air conditioners attached to the walls of apartments are very common in Hong Kong.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Road Signs
metas.note: • Road signs are white and rectangular, with a thick black outline and bilingual text.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Hong Kong usually uses white centre lines and white or yellow outer lines.
  • These lines can be single, double or dashed.
  • Yellow outer lines are most commonly found on small roads to indicate no-stopping.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Tall Buildings
metas.note:
• One very striking aspect of Hong Kong architecture are the many extremely tall apartment buildings found throughout the city.

--- NOTE:

  • Apartment buildings in Singapore and Taiwan tend to be not nearly as tall as those in Hong Kong.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Taxis
metas.note:
Hong Kong taxis come in two variants:

  • Sedans or station wagons, with the sedans most commonly seen.
  • They can be easily identified by their silver roofs, green stickers on the front and rear bumper, and the taxi sign on the roof.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hong Kong - Vibes
metas.note:
• Hong Kong is a densely populated city with millions of inhabitants.
  • In urban areas, modern skyscrapers are common, with busy streets filled with vehicles and pedestrians.
  • In many cases, this vibe alone should be sufficient to identify urban Hong Kong locations.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - 4 Bolt Signs
metas.note:
• Hungarian signs are usually bolted to the sign post using four bolts, going through the sign, in the shape of a tall rectangle.

--- NOTE:

  • This is not common in any other Eastern European countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Bollards
metas.note:
• Hungarian bollards are black-and-white, wedge-shaped, and typically have a red reflector at the front, and a white reflector at the back.

--- NOTE:

  • Croatian bollards are very similar.
  • They do, however, typically have the reflector closer to the top, and appear somewhat thinner than in Hungary.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Hungarian chevrons are white on red.
  • Black-and-white chevrons may also be seen, but are considerably less common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
• These green kilometre markers can be seen along most Hungarian roads.
  • On highways, the numbers correspond to the ones seen on the map in small yellow boxes near exits.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Poles
metas.note:
• The most common type of utility pole in Hungary is a concrete holey pole, with relatively thin holes going all the way down to the ground.

--- NOTE:

In eastern Europe, Poland and Romania also commonly use holey poles:

  • Polish holey poles typically do not have holes down by the ground, and tend to be relatively thin.
  • Romanian holey poles normally either have much wider, or much taller holes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Tall Sign Posts
metas.note: • Hungarian sign posts commonly appear to be abnormally tall, often taller than the Street View camera.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Iceland - Bollards
metas.note:
• Iceland has unique yellow bollards with a white reflector.
  • These bollards are extremely common and can be found throughout the country on almost every section of rural road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/iceland for more clues.

metas.name: Iceland - Gen 3 White Car Antenna
metas.note: • The Generation 3 Google car in Iceland is a white car with a long antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/iceland for more clues.

metas.name: Iceland - Gen 4 Blurred Truck
metas.note: • The Generation 4 coverage was captured with red and white pickup trucks, which have been well blurred.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/iceland for more clues.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape
metas.note:
• Iceland is a very geologically active country, where plate tectonics and volcanic processes have shaped the landscape.
  • As a result, many regions are rugged, mountainous and a sight to behold.
  • In addition, strange and bewildering landscapes can be found all over, such as geothermal lakes, lava fields, rift valleys, and towering rock formations.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/iceland for more clues.

metas.name: Iceland - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note:
• Icelandic pedestrian signs feature four stripes and often have a slight yellow tint.

--- NOTE:

  • Iceland is the only European country that uses pedestrian signs with a yellow background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/iceland for more clues.

metas.name: India - License Plates
metas.note:
• Indian licence plates are typically fairly long, with the most common design being white.
  • Commercial vehicles typically use yellow plates, while electric vehicles use green.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Shitcam
metas.note:
• The vast majority of the coverage in India was taken with what’s commonly referred to as “shitcam”.
  • It's a low-quality camera that can typically be recognised by the brownish colours and often, but not always, by a large circular blur covering the Street View car.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, shitcam coverage is also common in Cambodia and can rarely be seen in Sri Lanka and Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• India typically has black and white striped signposts.

--- NOTE:

  • Bangladesh and Sri Lanka also have black and white signposts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Indonesia commonly uses these black-and-white square or circular bollards, as well as these yellow-and-black ones, which can also have a red reflector.
  • Other designs can also be found.

--- NOTE:

  • UK-style bollards are mostly found in Kalimantan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - License Plates
metas.note:
• Indonesian licence plates are black with white letters.
  • The letters usually appear as three white sections through the blur.
  • Plates in newer coverage can be white too.

--- NOTE:

  • Malaysian licence plates are also black, but generally have two white sections.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Motorcycle Front Plates
metas.note: • Motorcycles in Indonesia have front licence plates, as opposed to other south-east Asian countries which do not.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Poles
metas.note:
• Poles in Indonesia are typically round and made out of either steel or concrete.
  • Many of the steel poles are painted black, and also feature the Indonesian flag colours on them.
  • The pole tops are usually either even or uneven, depending on the region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Indonesia uses white or yellow centre lines.
  • Outer lines will always be white.
  • The centre lines will be solid or dashed.

--- NOTE:

  • In Generation 3 coverage, yellow centre lines are more rare, as Indonesia only recently started using this colour for its road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Black Roofs
metas.note:
• You will usually find cream white buildings with black roofs in Ireland.
  • Sometimes, the buildings feature grey corner stones.
  • In cities, you will typically find row buildings.

--- NOTE:

  • British style brick buildings can still be found in Ireland.--
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Bollards
metas.note:
• These green and white bollards can be a good clue for Ireland.
  • They are not entirely unique to the country, but they are especially helpful in 50-50s with the UK.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Irish chevrons are yellow on black.
  • Both single and multiple arrows are common.

--- NOTE:

  • UK chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Diamond Warning Signs
metas.note:
• Ireland is the only European country that uses yellow diamond-shaped warning signs.

--- NOTE:

  • This only applies to warning signs.
  • Regulatory signs (circles and upside down triangles) have the normal red border and white background, like most other European countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - EU Plates
metas.note:
• Ireland has long, white licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • The white backplate is especially useful to distinguish it from the UK, which uses yellow backplates (but white fronts).
  • In addition, most UK vehicles lack the blue strip on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Pole Warning Signs
metas.note:
• The yellow warning stickers on utility poles can be a good way to distinguish between Ireland and the UK.
  • The most important difference is that UK stickers feature a guy getting zapped by a lightning bolt.

--- NOTE:

  • The Irish stickers usually have a lightning bolt, but lack the guy getting zapped.
  • They also often have an extra second rectangular sticker with a black outline, below the lightning bolt.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Rounded Metal Gates
metas.note:
• Rural metal gates with rounded corners are very common in Ireland.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mainly useful to distinguish it from the UK, where similar gates typically have square corners.
  • However, gates in Northern Ireland also typically have rounded corners.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Strip Of Grass
metas.note:
• You will often see a strip of grass in the middle of tiny rural roads.
  • Such roads are called “boreens”.
  • While not unique, these boreens can often be a strong clue in a tough 50-50 between Ireland and the UK.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Yellow Dashed Outlines
metas.note:
• It is very common to see yellow outside dashes on Irish roads.

--- NOTE:

  • This is essentially never found in the UK.
  • These dashes can also be seen in New Zealand.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Yield
metas.note:
• Irish yield signs feature the word “YIELD”.

--- NOTE:

  • UK yield signs have the phrase “GIVE WAY”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Isle of Man - Gen 2
metas.note:
• Coverage on the Isle of Man is limited to Generation 2.
  • This camera can be recognized by the lower camera quality and circular blur above and below.
  • Colours will also seem slightly off.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Isle of Man - Landscape
metas.note: • The general landscape on the Isle of Man consists of hilly farmland, and narrow roads passing through them.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Isle of Man - Red Strip Yellow Plates
metas.note: • Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a red strip on the left.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are white on black.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Curbs
metas.note:
• You will very often see striped kerbs.
  • Red and white and fairly commonly black and white.
  • Red and yellow and blue and white are also rarely found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note:
• Most Generation 3 coverage was taken by a black Street View car with a long antenna.
  • You may also see the black car without an antenna and a silver car with a short antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Kilometre Markers
metas.note: • Kilometre markers are white with a thick border, which can either be red, green or blue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - License Plates
