metas.note:
• Israeli licence plates are yellow with a blue strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • While this design is specific for Israel, it is also very common on the West Bank.
  • Jordan and the UAE use white licence plates.
  • Tunisia uses black plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Painted Poles
metas.note: • Utility poles commonly feature these painted black and white striped bottoms.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Roadlines
metas.note: • Most roads feature yellow outer lines with white centre lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Stop Sign
metas.note: • Rather than having a word meaning ‘stop’ written on them, stop signs have a hand painted on them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Architecture
metas.note:
• Italian architecture mainly consists of pastel coloured stone houses, generally with terracotta roofs.
  • Houses will very commonly have wooden shutters, which will typically be divided in two and open sideways.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Bollards
metas.note:
• Italian bollards are triangular in shape, and white with a black top.
  • They have a red front and a white rear reflector.

--- NOTE:

  • Albania uses the same bollards.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Italian chevrons are white arrows on a black background.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southern Europe, white on black chevrons can also be found in Spain, Greece and Albania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Double Guardrails
metas.note: • It is very common to find double guardrails in Italy.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Guardrail Endings
metas.note:
• Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape.
  • The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - License Plates
metas.note:
• Contrary to most European licence plates, Italian plates have blue strips on either side of the plate.
  • Furthermore, the front plate is distinctly shorter than most European plates, which in combination with the two strips, makes it unique.

--- NOTE:

  • Albanian licence plates also have two blue strips, and French licence plates have a smaller strip on the right.
  • However, neither Albanian nor French front plates are short.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Red Reflectors
metas.note:
• Italian guardrails feature red front reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • This is most useful to distinguish Italy from Spain, which uses yellow reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Roadlines
metas.note:
• One of the most common types of Italian road lines are white solid outer lines with no middle line.
  • This is generally less common in other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Trident Pole Tops
metas.note:
• The most common pole tops in Italy are concrete trident pole tops.
  • There are several possible configurations of insulators.
  • The two shown in the image are the most common ones.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Via & Street Signs
metas.note:
• Street signs are typically white with a thin blue border and black text.
  • The name for “Road” or “Way” in Italian is Via.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - White Pole Sticker
metas.note: • Wooden poles in Italy will commonly feature a small white pole sticker.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture
metas.note:
• Japanese architecture has many distinct and expressive styles, with many unique buildings.
  • These can range from traditional country houses, regional designs, modern large cities, coastal reinforced buildings, and anything in between.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Bollards
metas.note:
• Japan usually uses simple white bollards with circular reflector(s) on the top.
  • However, sometimes these bollards are black, or have other extensions.
  • They can also have the city or prefecture written on it in kanji.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Japan uses a standard short white licence plate with green text.
  • You will often see a different short yellow version with black text issued to “light automobiles”, otherwise known as Kei Cars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Lowcam
metas.note:
Due to privacy reasons, the camera is intentionally set lower to the ground.

This is known as low-cam.

You can identify it by:

  • Looking downwards.
  • The blur will be noticeably larger.
  • The road will look wider, and objects will be viewed from a lower perspective.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Poles
metas.note:
Japan mostly uses these round concrete poles, which have these screw-like extensions.

Other information can often be found on or attached to the pole including:

  • Electrical plates.
  • Guy-wires.
  • Pole reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Retaining Walls
metas.note: • Retaining walls can be an excellent clue for Japan in rural areas with little to no information.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Jersey - Landscape
metas.note:
• The island is shaped by a unique mix of British and Norman influences.
  • The many winding roads and hedgerows are reminiscent of English country lanes, with tree-covered roads being particularly common.
  • All images were taken by a Generation 2 camera.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Jersey - Red Granite
metas.note:
• Jersey is home to large reserves of red granite.
  • As a result, it is a popular building material used for the construction of many walls and houses throughout the island.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Architecture
metas.note:
• Most buildings in Jordan are made of bright sandstone bricks and have flat roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar sandstone bricks are also common in Jerusalem.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Black Car
metas.note:
• Coverage in Jordan was taken by a black Google car, without a red brake light.

--- NOTE:

  • Jordan is the only Middle Eastern country where a black Google car without an antenna or a red brake light can be found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Jordanian chevrons are white with red arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • You can use chevrons to distinguish between Jordan and Israel:
  • The Israeli chevrons are black with white arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Jordanian licence plates are white and can be long or short.
  • Commercial transport vehicles, such as taxis, have a distinctive green strip on the left.

--- NOTE:

  • In the Middle East, the green strip is only found in Jordan.
  • The UAE also uses long white plates.
  • Israel however only uses yellow licence plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Jordan typically feature yellow outside and white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Other Middle Eastern countries such as the UAE and Israel can also have these road lines.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Bollards
metas.note:
• Kazakhstan uses a variety of post-Soviet style bollards, as well as ones that resemble Turkish bollards.
  • Notably, the bollards seemingly consisting of two thin bollards attached at a 90° angle are unique to Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Car
metas.note: • All of the coverage in Kazakhstan was taken with a white pickup truck, which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Gas Pipes
metas.note: • Gas pipes are extremely common in Kazakh cities.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Landscape
metas.note:
• Kazakhstan is a big and diverse country, which features a plethora of distinct landscapes like deserts, grassy steppes, mountain passes, and birch forests.
  • Most strikingly, most of the rural coverage in Kazakhstan is in a very empty, open and mostly flat landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Pedestrian Crossing
metas.note:
• Like Russia, Kazakhstan uses yellow and white stripes on their pedestrian crossings.
  • However, unlike Russia the stripes often have white dashes on either side.
  • Sometimes, you can find the dashes without the stripes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kazakhstan - Russian Infrastructure
metas.note: • A lot of Kazakh infrastructure, from pedestrian signs, poles, houses, to bollards, is very similar to what you see in Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kazakhstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Follow Car
metas.note: • On a lot of the coverage you will see a grey Toyota SUV following the Street View car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Gen 4 Cars
metas.note:
• Kenya has many unique Google cars, almost all of which will have visible car meta.
  • In Generation 3 you will typically see a car with a roof rack and a snorkel.
  • In Generation 4 you will always have a large pickup truck, which will either be white or grey.
  • The grey car comes in two slightly different variations, of which one can either be with or without a snorkel.

--- NOTE:

  • It is the only country other than Mongolia with a snorkel.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - License Plates
metas.note:
• Kenya uses long white front licence plates.
  • The rear counterpart is square and yellow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Roadlines
metas.note: • Outer lines in Kenya will always be solid white, while inner lines will be yellow and either solid or dashed.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Bollards
metas.note: • Kyrgyzstan uses these simple white bollards with a diagonal black stripe near the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Car
metas.note:
• Kyrgyzstan can be recognised from the silver car and four bars that are visible.
  • All coverage is Generation 3.

--- NOTE:

  • No other country with a similar landscape has a similar Street View car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Landscape
metas.note: • All of Kyrgyzstan was covered during the winter months, so many of the trees will lack leaves, the landscape will be quite drab, and you can see snow in many parts of Kyrgyzstan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - License Plates
metas.note:
• Licence plates in Kyrgyzstan have a red strip on them.

--- NOTE:

  • Licence plates with red strips can sometimes be seen in Albania and very rarely in the UAE.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Laos - License Plates
metas.note:
• Laotian licence plates are short and yellow.
  • This distinguishes them from nearby Thailand and Cambodia, who both use white plates on non-commercial vehicles.
  • Laotian commercial plates are white, and government plates are blue.

--- NOTE:

  • Thailand uses yellow plates for commercial vehicles, such as taxis.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/laos for more clues.

metas.name: Laos - Unique Car
metas.note:
• In all cities except for the capital, Vientiane, this Google car will be visible.
  • It is silver-coloured, with a roof rack with two metal bars and black side mirrors.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar car can be found in Guatemala, so be sure to look at the other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/laos for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Latvian bollards have a thin, slightly curved shape.
  • They have a rectangular reflector on the front, and two circular reflectors on the back.
  • The reflectors can be white or orange.
  • The black strip is slightly angled.
  • Bollards often have numbers below the front reflector.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Bus Stop Sign
metas.note:
• The bus has five windows.
  • Within the Baltics, this is unique to Latvia.
  • The other two Baltic countries have four windows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Latvia uses white chevrons with red arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Many other European countries, including Lithuania and Poland, use the same chevrons.

However, Estonia, Russia and Ukraine use chevrons with the opposite colour scheme:

  • Red with white arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Hook Poles
metas.note:
• Latvian poles have distinctive poletops, with hook-shaped insulators, that are arranged in an alternating manner: left-right-left (or vice versa).

--- NOTE:

  • These poletops are much more rare in the other two Baltic countries.
  • They can however appear in some other European countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Iela
metas.note:
• The Latvian word for street is iela.
  • This word is unique to Latvian.
  • Very rarely, you might see ‘gatve’ in Riga (abbreviated as gat.).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
• All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.
  • However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
  • In Latvia, the marker will be parallel to the road.
  • It only has a number on one side.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Thick Red Border Signs
metas.note:
• Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
  • Latvian signs have a thick red border, with a thin white outline around it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - White & Red Reflectors
metas.note:
• Latvia has normal A-type guardrails with white or red reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • Estonia has no reflectors.
  • Lithuania has orange reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Agave Plants
metas.note: • These agave plants are common throughout the countryside and often a good clue for the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Architecture
metas.note:
• In rural areas, you will often see traditional round huts with thatched roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • These are less common in the other three southern African countries, but can still be seen.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Landscape
metas.note:
• One of the best ways to identify the country are the characteristic ‘Lesotho mountains’.
  • They are bare and treeless, often have tabletop-like shapes, and recognizable horizontal rocky ridgelines.

--- NOTE:

  • Depending on where you are in the country, the mountains can vary a bit in appearance.
  • Especially inland areas towards the southeast, where they appear more like rolling green hills rather than isolated tabletop mountains.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Lesotho uses yellow outer lines and white inner lines.

--- NOTE:

  • These are also found in the other three southern African countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Short Grass
metas.note:
• Grasslands in Lesotho primarily consist of short grass.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mostly useful to distinguish Lesotho from Eswatini, which famously has a lot of tall grass.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - White Car
metas.note:
• All coverage in Lesotho is Generation 3.
  • In almost all locations, the back of a white Google car without an antenna is visible.

--- NOTE:

  • The other three southern African countries of Eswatini, Botswana and South Africa also have the same white car in Generation 3 coverage.
  • Generation 3 in South Africa is fairly rare.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Bollards
metas.note:
• Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped.
  • They have an orange reflector on the front, and a white reflector on the back.
  • Both reflectors are rectangular.
  • You may find this thin version as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Lithuania uses white chevrons with red arrows.
  • The small single chevrons (pictured here) usually have a red outline on the edge of the sign.

--- NOTE:

  • Many other European countries, including Latvia and Poland, use the same chevrons (though without the red outline).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - G.
metas.note:
• The Lithuanian word for street is gatve, often abbreviated as g. on signs and Google Maps.
  • This word is almost entirely unique to Lithuanian.
  • However, very rarely, you might see gat. in the Latvian capital of Riga.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
• All Baltic countries use the same blue kilometre marker.
  • However, they can be distinguished from each other by their angle relative to the road.
  • In Lithuania, the marker will be at a 45° angle towards the road.
  • The sign itself has an L-shape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Less Forest Cover
metas.note:
• Lithuania has less forest cover than the other two Baltic countries.
  • As a result, the landscape appears more open and agricultural.
  • Your mileage may vary depending on the round however, so use this meta with some caution.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Orange Reflectors
metas.note:
• Lithuania has normal A-type guardrails with orange reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • Estonia has no reflectors.
  • Latvia has red or white reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Pole Tops
metas.note:
• Pictured here are some typical Lithuanian poletops.
  • They often have short horizontal rods, on which the insulators are placed.
  • In some poletops, the insulators are arranged in a trident-like shape, with one on top, and two on each side.

--- NOTE:

These poletops are not unique to Lithuania:

  • They can also be found in the other post-Soviet countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Square Poles
metas.note:
• Lithuanian poles are usually square and concrete, and often feature a diagonal support beam.

--- NOTE:

  • While most common in Lithuania, these are also found from time to time in Estonia, and on rare occasions in Latvia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Lithuania - Thin Red Border Signs
metas.note:
• Each Baltic country has a slightly different border for its warning and speed signs.
  • Lithuanian signs have a relatively thin red border, with a thin white outline around it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lithuania for more clues.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Bollards
metas.note:
• Bollards are black and white.
  • They are wedge-shaped and have grey reflectors. Some have a distinctive indent in the lower half.

--- NOTE:

  • They look more or less identical to German bollards.
  • The most notable difference is that the reflectors on German bollards have two bolts, while in Luxembourg they have three.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/luxembourg for more clues.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Chevrons are black with yellow arrows.
  • You may also rarely come across blue and yellow chevrons.

--- NOTE:

  • None of Luxembourg’s neighbours use these chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/luxembourg for more clues.

metas.name: Luxembourg - White Signposts
metas.note:
• Almost all Luxembourgish road signs will be supported by a white signpost.

--- NOTE:

  • While not nearly as common, white signposts are also found in France.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/luxembourg for more clues.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Yellow Plates
metas.note:
• Luxembourg uses long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left.
  • Since Luxembourg is a small country, foreign cars with white plates are somewhat common.

--- NOTE:

  • There are only a few other European countries that use yellow plates for private vehicles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/luxembourg for more clues.

metas.name: Macau - Gen 2
metas.note:
• Coverage in Macau is limited to Generation 2.
  • Generation 2 can be recognized by the lower camera quality and circular blur above and below the camera.
  • The coverage in Macau specifically is some of the oldest Generation 2 available, meaning that the colours look even more washed out and overexposed than usual.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Macau - License Plates
metas.note:
• Macau uses black licence plates with white text.
  • Licence plates can either be long or square.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Madeira - Concrete Blocks
metas.note: • Concrete block barriers, usually painted white, are often found along roads.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Madeira - Eucalyptus Forests
metas.note:
• Similar to continental Portugal, Madeira has a lot of eucalyptus forests, which can sometimes look deceptively like the mainland.

--- NOTE:

  • The Azores do not commonly have eucalypti.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Madeira - Mountainous Landscape
metas.note:
• Madeira is a very mountainous and semi-tropical island.

--- NOTE:

  • The Azores are less mountainous and more temperate.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Madeira - Portuguese Infrastructure
metas.note: • Since Madeira is an autonomous region of Portugal, you will often come across various types of Portuguese infrastructure, such as poles and chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Madeira - Stone Bollards
metas.note:
• Madeira commonly uses small and unique stone bollards with a red reflector.
  • They are either cuboidal or cylindrical in shape.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Malaysian bollards will often have the colours black, white, grey and red.

--- NOTE:

  • There can be multiple varieties of these bollards, but the layout is mostly the same.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Directional Signs
metas.note:
• This is a typical Malaysian directional sign.
  • Hexagonal yellow highway shields are unique to Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - License Plates
metas.note:
• Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections.
  • These are visible even when blurred.

--- NOTE:

  • Indonesian licence plates are also black, but they will have three white sections.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• Electricity poles in Malaysia often have black or white stickers on them.
  • Sometimes you will also find red-and-white or red-and-blue stripes below the black sticker.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Malaysia frequently uses double white centre lines on its two-lane roads.
  • It is the only Southeast Asian country to do so.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Stop Sign
metas.note: • BERHENTI stop signs and BERI LALUAN yield signs are both unique to Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Malaysia almost always have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South-East Asia, these posts are also found in Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
  • Make sure to check other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Yellow Bars
metas.note:
• These thick yellow bars are also almost exclusive to Malaysia.

--- NOTE:

  • You can very rarely see similar patterns in Hong Kong and the United Kingdom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Architecture
metas.note:
• The vast majority of buildings in Malta consist of low storey buildings, with white to beige coloured walls.
  • Buildings made of limestone are also fairly common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Landscape
metas.note:
• The general landscape of Malta consists of slightly hilly dry agricultural fields.
  • Many roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide, due to the island’s size.
  • Having a mediterranean climate, cacti and various dry shrubs can be seen.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Left Driving Side
metas.note: • Malta drives on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Rock Walls
metas.note:
• Limestone rock walls are extremely common in Malta.
  • This alone is usually enough to determine that you are in Malta.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Triq
metas.note: • The Maltese word for street is “triq”, which can be seen on almost every street sign.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - ALTO
metas.note:
• Mexico uses the word “ALTO” on stop signs.

--- NOTE:

  • All of South America uses the word “PARE”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Black & White Water Tanks
metas.note: • You will commonly see wide cylindrical, black or white water tanks on rooftops.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Bollards
metas.note: • These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector can sometimes be seen, as well as a flat version.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Cacti
metas.note: • Cacti, of many different species, are extremely common in Mexico.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Electricity Counters
metas.note:
• Mexico uses circular electricity counters.

--- NOTE:

  • Circular electricity counters are not unique to Mexico and can also be found in the US, Guatemala, Dominican Republic and the Philippines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
The Generation 3 coverage in Mexico mainly feature two cars:

  • A white car with a stubby antenna.
  • A white car with a more visible back and a long red brake light

--- NOTE:

  • It is possible to find a white car without a stubby antenna, but with a tiny sliver visible where the antenna should be.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - License Plates
metas.note:
• Mexico uses short licence plates with a large variety of designs.
  • Front plates are required.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Octagonal Pole
metas.note:
• Most utility poles in Mexico are made of concrete and have an octagonal shape.
  • There will often be engravings on the side.

--- NOTE:

  • Octagonal poles are also common in Colombia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Thick Arrows
metas.note: • Arrows on signs are noticeably very thick.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Monaco - Palm Trees
metas.note: • Planted palm trees are common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/monaco for more clues.

metas.name: Monaco - Vibe
metas.note:
• Monaco is a rich and densely populated city state, with a Mediterranean feel to it.
  • The architecture is similar to cities in southern France and northern Italy, but more luxurious.
  • You will see a lot of apartment buildings, neoclassical details, and pastel colours.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/monaco for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Bollards
metas.note: • Mongolia uniquely features white bowling-pin shaped bollards with two red stripes around the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Cars
metas.note:
• Mongolia very often has a visible Street View car as all of Mongolian coverage was driven with a large pickup truck.
  • The truck can have several features such as a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks.
  • All of these can be of help in identifying Mongolia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Landscape
metas.note:
• Mongolia can typically be identified by the steppe biomes found across the country.
  • While some forested areas are found in Mongolia, most of the country features empty grasslands or deserts with a characteristic lack of trees.

--- NOTE:

  • It is not uncommon to find rugged, rocky or rolling hills as well as rivers and lakes across Mongolia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Round Yurts
metas.note: • White, round yurts are the traditional dwelling of nomadic families in Mongolia, and are often seen all around the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Montenegro - Bollards
metas.note:
• The most common bollard is white with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.
  • The bollard also has a black top.

--- NOTE:

  • These bollards are also found in Slovenia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/montenegro for more clues.

metas.name: Montenegro - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Montenegro uses black on white or red on yellow chevrons.

--- NOTE:

  • Albania uses white on black chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/montenegro for more clues.

metas.name: Montenegro - Mountainous Landscape
metas.note:
• Montenegro is a small, mountainous country.
  • Inland mountains are lush and green, while most coastal mountains have distinct exposed, light coloured rock.
  • Most roads are also only 1 or 2 lanes wide.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/montenegro for more clues.

metas.name: Montenegro - Rifts
metas.note:
• ‘Rifts’ can commonly be seen in Montenegrin coverage, due to poor stitching.

--- NOTE:

  • Rifts are also common in Albania, and can rarely be seen in various other countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/montenegro for more clues.

metas.name: Montenegro - Rusty Guardrails
metas.note: • Guardrails in Montenegro are often rusted.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/montenegro for more clues.

metas.name: Montenegro - Thin Font Signs
metas.note:
• The numbers on speed signs are written in a thin font.

--- NOTE:

  • The font is much thicker on speed signs in Albania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/montenegro for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bicycle Paths
metas.note:
• Many Dutch roads are flanked by bicycle paths.
  • Different designs exist, but a very common one is a reddish-pink lane.
  • Cycling is one of the most common modes of transportation in the Netherlands.
  • You will see cyclists and bicycles everywhere.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bollards
metas.note:
• The Netherlands has a simple, white bollard with a red reflector.

--- NOTE:

  • On rare occasions, you can find round French-style bollards with a red band and a pointed top.
  • A difference with French bollards is that the red wrap usually does not go all the way around the bollard.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Brick Roads
metas.note:
• Brick roads are common in the Netherlands, both in rural and urban areas.
  • The brick pattern shown in the image is especially common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Bulky Yellow Signposts
metas.note: • Road signs on traffic islands often have these bulky yellow signposts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Flat Landscape
metas.note:
• The Netherlands is extraordinarily flat.
  • In most of the country, you will get no more than a few metres of elevation.
  • Large swathes of the country are reclaimed land that is at or even below sea level.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Gen 4 Black Back
metas.note: • Some Generation 4 coverage has a car blur glitch where the black back of the Google car is visible.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Large Power Lines
metas.note:
• The Netherlands usually does not have any utility poles.
  • You might see larger power lines like the ones shown in the image, but essentially never any street-level smaller utility poles.

--- NOTE:

  • Belgium does use utility poles somewhat commonly.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Rumble Strips
metas.note:
• Many rural roads feature a sort of brick rumble strip on the sides.
  • This is fairly unique to the Netherlands and a good way to identify the country in very rural rounds.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Yellow Plates
metas.note:
• The Netherlands has long, yellow licence plates with the standard European blue strip on the left.
  • Dutch taxis have blue plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Bollards
metas.note:
• Bollards in New Zealand have a red strip which wraps around the top of the bollard.
  • This strip wraps the whole way around the back and part of the front.

--- NOTE:

  • These bollards are unique to New Zealand.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Poles
metas.note:
• The most common pole type found in New Zealand is made of concrete and has one long indent which runs most of the way up the pole.
  • Most concrete poles have small silver possum guards.
  • You can also see concrete holey poles in New Zealand.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Red Give-Way Sign
metas.note:
• Give-way signs in New Zealand have a white border and red text.

--- NOTE:

  • Australia’s give-way signs use black text.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Street Signs
metas.note:
• New Zealand often uses blue street signs with white text, particularly in rural areas.
  • While street signs of other colours can be often seen, blue is by far the most common.

--- NOTE:

  • Australia almost never has blue street signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Architecture
metas.note:
• Most Nigerian houses are single-storey, with steeply pitched roofs commonly made of metal sheets.
  • Cinder block walls surrounding the houses are also common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Follow Car
metas.note:
• A police car, most commonly white or black, can almost always be seen following the Street View car.
  • The follow cars may differ slightly from the ones shown in the image.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• A visible Street View car is present in most of the coverage, being a pickup truck with the cab and bed visible.
  • The colour of the cab and other features of it varies. In Generation 3, a roof rack is present.

--- NOTE:

  • You may also find a large blur covering the entire pickup truck.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - License Plates
metas.note: • Nigeria uses short licence plates that appear somewhat green through the blur.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Poles
metas.note:
• Most Nigerian poles are made of concrete.
  • They have indents with a few horizontal supports, and are similar to the ones used in Brazil, but do not have holes through them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Nigeria - Shitcam
metas.note: • Within mainland Africa, Nigeria is currently the only country to have this low-quality coverage, known as official ari, or “shitcam”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: North Macedonia - Bollards
metas.note:
• North Macedonia uses two types of bollards.
  • One is rounded and very thin, while the other one is wedge-shaped.
  • They both are white and have red or white reflectors, typically on a black surface.

--- NOTE:

  • Croatia uses the same wedge-shaped bollard.
  • Hungary has a similar wedge-shaped bollard but with more white space above the black rectangle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/north-macedonia for more clues.

metas.name: North Macedonia - Dry Grasslands
metas.note: • The general landscape of North Macedonia consists of relatively dry grasslands, and small hills and scattered trees.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/north-macedonia for more clues.

metas.name: North Macedonia - Gen 3 No Antenna
metas.note:
• All coverage in North Macedonia is Generation 3.
  • There will never be an antenna on the Google car.
  • Every other country in Europe will sometimes or always have an antenna in Generation 3 coverage.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other country to have no antenna the majority of the time is Serbia, although there will be an antenna sometimes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/north-macedonia for more clues.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Close Antenna
metas.note:
• The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right can be seen.
  • The antenna is also noticeably closer to the camera than in the Guam Google car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands for more clues.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Poles
metas.note:
• Northern Mariana Islands have wooden poles, frequently with a crossbar at the top.

--- NOTE:

  • Guam typically has concrete poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands for more clues.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Road Reflectors
metas.note: • Both Northern Mariana Islands and Guam often have a very large number of road reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Architecture
metas.note:
• Many houses are painted red, which is also typical for Sweden and Finland.
  • Black painted houses are also quite common, more so than in Sweden or Finland.

--- NOTE:

  • Sweden and Finland generally have more red and yellow houses, while Norway generally has more white houses.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Bollards
metas.note: • Norway uses thin, curved rectangular bollards with the reflector inside of a black parallelogram.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Centered Top Sign Posts
metas.note:
• Street signs will generally be centred on top of sign posts.

--- NOTE:

  • Street signs in Sweden will normally be attached either to the side of sign posts or lamp posts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Chevrons
metas.note: • Norway uses yellow on black chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Guardrail Wooden Posts
metas.note:
• Guardrails often have wooden posts.

--- NOTE:

  • This is not common in Sweden or Finland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape
metas.note:
• Norway is a very mountainous country, with many fjords along most of the coast.

--- NOTE:

  • Finland and Denmark are both mostly flat, while Sweden has a mixture of flat, hilly and mountainous areas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - License Plates
metas.note:
• Norway has long white licence plates with the standard European strip on the left.
  • Commercial plates are green.
  • These are often seen on vans.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Europe, green licence plates are most commonly seen in Norway, but also on electric vehicles in Hungary.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Long Dashed Roadlines
metas.note:
• Smaller Norwegian roads typically have long dashed white outer lines, while larger roads have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines.
  • The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange.

--- NOTE:

  • Sweden only has white road lines, and the dashes on outer lines are shorter than in Norway.
  • Finnish outer road lines are always solid, and middle lines can be yellow or white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Small Dot Roadlines
metas.note: • Road lines will often be made up of small dots of paint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Snow Poles
metas.note:
• Norwegian snow poles are typically orange, with a fairly thin white reflector.
  • The reflector is normally toward the middle of the pole.

--- NOTE:

  • Swedish snow poles typically have a wider reflector slightly higher up, and Finnish snow poles have their reflector at the very top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Traffic Signs
metas.note:
• Norwegian traffic signs have a red outline and a white background.

--- NOTE:

  • Both Swedish and Finnish road signs have a yellow background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Car
metas.note: • All the coverage in Oman was taken with a white pickup truck, meaning you will either see most of the car or a large front blur.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Chevrons
metas.note: • Oman uses black-and-yellow chevrons that have an unusually large number of arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Curbs
metas.note:
• Black-and-yellow curbs are common in Oman.

--- NOTE:

  • The UAE also commonly uses similar curbs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Garbage Bins
metas.note:
• The vast majority of garbage bins in Oman are either black and made of plastic or metallic and grey, with a three-leaf logo and the text ‘be’ah’ below it.

--- NOTE:

  • Garbage bins in the UAE will occasionally have the text “bee’ah”, with two E’s.
  • The bins are often more colourful too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - High Voltage Pylons
metas.note:
• High voltage pylons painted with a red and white pattern are common in Oman.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Middle East, red and white painted pylons can also less commonly be found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Landscape
metas.note:
• Most of Oman features a desert landscape with little vegetation.
  • While the middle and southern half is mostly flat, the north coast features dry mountains similar to those found in the UAE.
  • The southern coast also has mountains, though less dry.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - License Plates
metas.note: • Licence plates on private vehicles are generally yellow, while commercial vehicles have red plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Roads in Oman use yellow outer and white middle lines.

--- NOTE:

  • This is also common in the UAE, Israel, Jordan, as well as occasionally found in Qatar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Oman - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Many signposts in Oman have black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • Within the Middle East, striped signposts are only found in Oman and the UAE.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/oman for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - Architecture
metas.note:
• Panamanian architecture often reflects Spanish colonial influences, featuring vibrant colours, and some ornate detailing.
  • The most common type of building has painted concrete or sometimes brick walls with red metal sheets or tiles for a roof.
  • Many windows have bars on them for security.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - Big Font ALTO
metas.note:
• Panama uses the Spanish word “ALTO” on stop signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Mexico and Guatemala also use “ALTO”, but the font is thinner.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - License Plates
metas.note:
• Panama features short licence plates, most commonly white with a horizontal turquoise strip on the top.
  • Rarely, the strip can have other colours.
  • Front plates are not required in Panama.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - Small Tree Fences
metas.note:
• Most roads are paralleled by fences that are partly or fully made out of small trees.
  • The rest of the fence posts are also almost always wooden.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: Panama - White Truck
metas.note:
• Panama features a large white pickup truck which can either be fully visible or mostly blurred.
  • There is always a short black antenna attached to the front of the car.
  • Beware that the antenna can sometimes be blurred.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/panama for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Black & White Car
metas.note:
• In Gen 3 coverage, Peru uses a black and a white Google car.

--- NOTE:

In South America, these two cars are limited to the following countries:

  • The black Google car is only found in Peru, Argentina and Uruguay.
  • The white Google car is only found in Peru, Bolivia and Chile.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Bollards
metas.note:
• Bollards in Peru are painted red or yellow, and the country mainly uses a variety of triangular-shaped concrete bollards.
  • Occasionally you will also spot other designs, such as these circular concrete variants.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Concrete Blocks
metas.note:
• Peruvian metal signposts feature concrete blocks at the bottom.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South America, Peru is the only country to do so.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
• Kilometre markers in Peru are made out of concrete and are painted black and white.

--- NOTE:

  • When entering and leaving urban areas, the markers will sometimes feature the road number.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Striped Guardrails
metas.note:
• Black-and-yellow stripes on guardrails are seen throughout the country.
  • You might sometimes find different designs, such as this sharp arrow design.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar striped guardrails are also found in Bolivia.
  • To differentiate them, just have a look at the outer stripe.
  • Peru uses a black one, while Bolivia features a yellow one.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Peru often has black-and-white striped signposts.
  • In some areas, black-and-yellow signposts can be seen.

--- NOTE:

  • It is the only country in South America that uses them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Tuk Tuks
metas.note:
Tuk tuks, called mototaxis in Peru, are frequently seen in the country, especially in major cities such as:

  • Lima
  • Trujillo
  • Chiclayo
  • Piura Iquitos
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Chevrons
metas.note: • Chevrons are typically red on white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Concrete Roads
metas.note:
• Concrete roads are extremely common in the Philippines.

--- NOTE:

  • Thailand also has a lot of concrete roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Gen 3 Black Roof
metas.note:
• In Generation 3 you can come across a white Street View car with the black roof clearly visible.
  • You may also come across a silvery grey car, which is also found in Bhutan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Poles
metas.note:
• Octagonal metal poles are quite common in the Philippines.

--- NOTE:

  • They can sometimes be found in Bangladesh and some parts of Malaysia as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle road lines in the Philippines can be either yellow or white.
  • In particular, you will often see combined yellow and white middle lines, which is not common in any other East Asian country.
  • Yellow road lines commonly have a distinct orange tint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Single Insulator
metas.note: • You will often see a single insulator at the top of a vertical bar which is attached to the side of a utility pole.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Tuk-Tuks
metas.note: • Tuk-tuks, also referred to as tricycles, are extremely common in the Philippines, in many areas they are more common than typical cars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Bollards
metas.note:
• Polish bollards have a red strip that wraps all the way around the bollard.
  • This strip has a red reflector on the front (sometimes hard to see), and a white reflector on the back.
  • Bollards sometimes have numbers on them.

--- NOTE:

  • The same design can be found in Zakarpattia Oblast in Ukraine.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Double Roadlines
metas.note:
• Poland has all-white road lines.
  • Double middle lines are very common and usually a good clue for Poland.

--- NOTE:

  • Some other European countries, most notably Denmark and Greece, can have double middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Guardrail & Reflector
metas.note:
• Poland has square (normal B-type) guardrails, with circular red reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • Poland is one of only a very few European countries with this type of guardrail
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note:
• Poland has a unique pedestrian sign.
  • Instead of the usual zebra stripes, it just has a single horizontal line.

--- NOTE:

  • Austria and Belgium also have horizontal lines, but they use two lines instead of Poland’s single line.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Poles
metas.note:
• Poland usually has thin concrete utility poles with see-through holes.
  • The holes often do not extend all the way to the bottom of the pole.
  • You can also find round concrete poles.

--- NOTE:

  • Hungary and Romania also have holey poles, but these are wider and more bulky.
  • In addition, the holes extend all the way to the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Town Entry Signs
metas.note:
Poland has two town entry signs:

  • Agreen one with the locality’s name, and a white-and-black one with a stylized urban area.

--- NOTE:

  • Like direction signs, town entry signs use a distinct font.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Yellow Warning Signs
metas.note:
• Warning signs are triangular and have a yellow background and a distinct thin red border.

--- NOTE:

  • In Europe, this combination of a yellow background with a thin red border is unique to Poland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Architecture
metas.note: • White painted stone houses with orange tiled roofs are extremely common in Portugal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Bollards
metas.note:
• Portuguese bollards are either wedge-shaped with a noticeably thin white top, or flat with a wide reflector.
  • While most reflectors will be white, you may also find orange reflectors.
  • These are noticeably darker than the yellow reflectors in Spain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Portuguese chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Portugal is the only Mediterranean country with this chevron colour scheme.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Cobblestone Roads
metas.note:
• Cobblestone roads are very common in Portugal.
  • These will typically be made of square cobblestones arranged diagonally compared to the road direction.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Cobblestone Sidewalks
metas.note: • Similarly, cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Eucalyptus Trees
metas.note:
• Eucalyptus trees are very common in Portugal.
  • The only other part of Europe where you’ll commonly see eucalyptus is northern Spain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Hunting Signs
metas.note:
• Hunting signs with a red and white colour scheme are a common sight in rural areas.
  • They are either diamond shaped or rectangular.

--- NOTE:

  • In contrast, Spanish hunting signs are white and black.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Large Font Stop
metas.note:
• Stop signs in Portugal feature a fairly large font.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mostly useful to distinguish it from Spain, where stop signs have a distinctly small and compact font.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - License Plates
metas.note:
• Portuguese plates are long and white, with a blue strip on the left.
  • Most plates have a yellow strip on the right, which is unique to Portugal.
  • The yellow strip was discontinued in 2020, so in Generation 4 coverage you may sometimes see plates with just the blue strip.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Red Reflector
metas.note:
• Portugal uses A-type guardrails with red reflectors.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mostly useful to tell apart Portugal and Spain, which uses yellow reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Road Signs
metas.note:
• Portuguese road signs are typically encased by a white border.

--- NOTE:

  • Most Spanish signs don’t have a white border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Rua
metas.note:
• The Portuguese word for road is ‘Rua’.

--- NOTE:

  • In Galician, the word for road is ‘Rúa’, with an accent on the ‘u’.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Tall Ladder Poles
metas.note:
• Concrete ladder poles, with very tall ladder steps, are common in Portugal.
  • Each step often has a small see-through hole.

--- NOTE:

  • In Spain and France you will commonly see ladder poles with short steps.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - 787 Phone Code
metas.note:
• The entirety of Puerto Rico uses (787) as their regional phone code.

--- NOTE:

  • While far less common, you may also encounter the phone code 939.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico for more clues.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - No Front Plates
metas.note:
• Front plates are not mandatory in Puerto Rico.
  • Therefore, seeing cars with front plates is rare.
  • This helps differentiate from Guam and Northern Mariana Islands.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico for more clues.

metas.name: Puerto Rico - White Dot Antenna
metas.note:
• The Google Car found in Puerto Rico has an antenna at the front right.
  • The antenna has a small white dot on the tip.

--- NOTE:

  • The Google car on Guam and NMI also have an antenna at the front right.
  • Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/puerto-rico for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Car
metas.note:
• The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible.
  • Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible.
  • Rusty clips can be seen on the crossbar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Chevrons
metas.note: • Qatar uses white on red and white on blue chevrons.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Landscape
metas.note:
• Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, and mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see.
  • You will often not see a lot of trees or other greenery.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - License Plates
metas.note:
• Regular cars in Qatar have long, white licence plates with a maroon strip on the left.
  • Trucks have square, black licence plates and police plates are blue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note: • Qatari crossing signs feature a man in a thobe.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Poles
metas.note:
• Qatar uses round poles with 3 insulators on the pole top, with the middle one being slightly higher.
  • The crossbar also has 2 diagonal bars connecting it to the pole.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Qatar - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Qatar typically uses solid outer white lines with either white or yellow in the middle.
  • More rarely, you can also find outer yellow lines too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Réunion - French Infrastructure
metas.note: • Being a French Department, you will see French infrastructure, such as signs, bollards and poles.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Réunion - Unique Car
metas.note:
• Réunion has a Street View car with visible side mirrors, a roof rack, and black tape at the end of the rear right bar.

--- NOTE:

  • Make sure not to get this confused with the Ghana car, which has tape on the front right bar.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Romanian chevrons are red on white, often with a yellow frame.

--- NOTE:

  • Several eastern and central European countries have the red on white chevrons, however yellow frames are by far the most common in Romania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Dashed Roadlines
metas.note: • While there are many types of roadlines in Romania, these outer lines, consisting of short dashes with narrow spaces, can be a good clue for the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Large Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• This type of extremely large yellow pole sticker is specific to Romania.
  • Beware that smaller stickers are also common and that both Bulgaria and Hungary can have similar ones.

--- NOTE:

  • The town or city name will typically be written close to the middle of these stickers.
  • In this case Podu Iloaiei is written.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Painted Poles & Trees
metas.note:
• Trees and poles will often have white painted bottoms.

--- NOTE:

  • This is also common in Ukraine and parts of Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Poles
metas.note:
• The most common types of utility poles in Romania are holey poles with the holes going all the way to the bottom.
  • The holes are typically either quite wide or quite tall.

--- NOTE:

  • Poland and Hungary also both use holey poles.
  • Polish holey poles do not have holes near the bottom and Hungarian holey poles generally have smaller holes than in Romania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Thick Roadlines
metas.note:
• Middle lines are often noticeably thicker than average.
  • This is especially useful to tell Romania apart from Bulgaria, which generally has thinner road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Waystones
metas.note:
• It is very common to see waystones in Romania.
  • They are typically fairly large, with red or blue framing with the road number on the side, or made of actual stone and somewhat rugged-looking.
  • There is also a very small variant which is all white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Yield Sign
metas.note:
• This yield sign, with an extremely thick red border, with a thin white outline, is unique to Romania.
  • Beware that different yield signs also exist in Romania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Bollards
metas.note:
Russia has three main types of bollards:

  • A very thin type being attached to a stick.
  • One with a black top section.
  • A red vertical reflector below and a German-style bollard.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Decorated Windows
metas.note:
• This style of richly decorated window frames is commonly found on traditional Russian homes, especially on log cabins.
  • They are often painted blue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Gen 3 Cars
metas.note:
• Three Generation 3 Street View cars are commonly found in Russia.
  • The two most useful ones for recognising Russia are a black and a white car, both with a long antenna.
  • You may also see a short antenna without a visible car.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Large Apartments
metas.note:
• The vast majority of urban housing in Russia are large rectangular apartment buildings made of simple concrete.
  • Newer buildings in wealthier areas appear more modern.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Painted Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Russia often have black painted bottoms.

--- NOTE:

  • This is also common in Kazakhstan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Pedestrian Signs
metas.note:
• Russian pedestrian signs have a simply drawn person and three stripes.
  • Signs will commonly have a bright yellow border.

--- NOTE:

  • Ukraine, Lithuania, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan use the same design.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Rural Housing
metas.note: • Rural housing in Russia consists mostly of a basic wooden structure with metal roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Wide Intersections
metas.note: • Along with containing a large number of bollards, many intersections are unusually wide compared to other countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Architecture
metas.note:
• Rwandan architecture features a lot of brick and concrete.
  • Most houses in Rwanda are single family houses, which can have rather steep roofs.
  • Houses also often have fences for protection.

--- NOTE:

  • The most notable feature of Rwandan architecture are the ‘ventilation bricks,’ which are present in many houses.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Clean Roads
metas.note: • Streets in Rwanda are noticeably very clean and free of garbage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Curbs
metas.note: • Kerbs are often painted with black and white stripes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Hilly Landscape
metas.note: • Rwanda is generally quite hilly, but not very mountainous.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Motorcyclists
metas.note: • All motorcyclists in Rwanda are required to wear red vests and helmets.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Security Walls
metas.note: • Villa neighbourhoods often have a lot of tall security fences and walls.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: Rwanda - Unique Car
metas.note:
• All the coverage in Rwanda is made with a Generation 4 camera.

In most of the coverage, the Google car is entirely visible:

  • It is a big white, black, or brown pickup truck.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/rwanda for more clues.

metas.name: San Marino - Chevrons
metas.note: • San Marino uses yellow chevrons with burgundy red arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/san-marino for more clues.

metas.name: San Marino - Monte Titano
metas.note:
• The 739m-tall Monte Titano dominates the surrounding landscape and is visible from almost every point in the Republic.

--- NOTE:

  • Look for the three towers to safely identify it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/san-marino for more clues.

metas.name: São Tomé & Príncipe - Desaturated Shitcam
metas.note: • This desaturated and even dimmer variant of shitcam is most common on Príncipe.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: São Tomé & Príncipe - New Shitcam
metas.note:
• All the coverage was taken with a low quality camera that’s commonly referred to as “Shitcam”.

--- NOTE:

  • The coverage is a newer variant of shitcam, where the image is dimmer and hazier than the original shitcam primarily found in India and Nigeria.
  • Nigeria is also currently the only other country to have this newer variant.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: São Tomé & Príncipe - Portuguese Influence
metas.note:
Portuguese influence can be seen in:

  • Language.
  • Infrastructure, such as ladder poles.
  • Pedestrian signs with the same design as in Portugal.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: São Tomé & Príncipe - Rainforests
metas.note:
• São Tomé and Príncipe are tropical islands, which are almost completely covered in rainforests.
  • Banana plants are especially common throughout the islands.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - French Infrastructure
metas.note: • Being a former French colony, Senegal uses French infrastructure such as bollards, poles, signs and road lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Gen 4 Cars
metas.note:
• A silver or white truck cab is visible in the Generation 4 coverage.
  • The most useful and recognizable ones will be shown in the spotlight section.
  • In the area around Dakar and Thies you can also find a black pick up truck.

--- NOTE:

  • The car may sometimes be fully blurred.
  • Make sure to look at the landscape or other clues in the absence of car meta.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - License Plates
metas.note:
• Senegal is the only African country to use fully blue licence plates.
  • A newer version exists in Generation 4 which looks like the standard European licence plate which is white with a blue strip on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Solar Panel Lamps
metas.note: • These simple black lamps with a solar panel at the top are commonly seen in Senegal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Serbia - B-Type Guardrails
metas.note:
• Serbia uses B-Profile guardrails exclusively.

--- NOTE:

  • North Macedonia does not use B-Profile guardrails.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/serbia for more clues.

metas.name: Serbia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Serbia has a few bollard designs, however most of them will have an off-centred reflector.
  • The bollards are usually flat, with no depth to them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/serbia for more clues.

metas.name: Serbia - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Serbia uses chevrons with a black arrow on a white background.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Europe, these chevrons can also be found in Slovenia, Montenegro and North Macedonia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/serbia for more clues.

metas.name: Serbia - No Antenna
metas.note:
• Most of the coverage in Serbia was taken by a Google car with no antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • Other than North Macedonia, almost all of central and eastern Europe has antenna coverage in Generation 3.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/serbia for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Buses
metas.note:
• Singaporean buses are mostly lime-green, making them easily recognisable.
  • Other designs can also be found, for example the white-and-purple SBS Transit variants.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Road Signs
metas.note:
• Road signs in Singapore are unique in that they are always set on a square white background.

--- NOTE:

  • Road signs in almost all other countries will not have this square background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Street Signs
metas.note:
• All street name signs in Singapore follow this unique format.
  • They are green, with rounded edges and a distinct white font.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Vibes
metas.note:
• Singapore is a highly developed city-state, characterised by an overall cleanliness and orderliness.
  • Main roads are often divided, and commonly feature black-and-white curbs and double yellow outside lines.
  • You will often see tall apartment blocks nearby.

--- NOTE:

  • In many cases, this “general look” is all you need to easily identify Singapore.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Warnings On Roads
metas.note: • Warnings are often written on the road in large letters, such as the famous “HUMP AHEAD”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/singapore for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Big Font Road Signs
metas.note:
• Slovak road signs normally feature a very bold font.

--- NOTE:

  • The font on Czech signs is much thinner.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Bollards in Slovakia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back.
  • There are also rarer blue and red variants.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other country with the same design is Czechia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Direction Signs
metas.note:
• Slovakia uses blue directional signs, with small white arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Czechia has large filled in white arrows instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - House Numbers
metas.note: • House numbers in Slovakia are typically written on white signs with a thin red or black border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Mountainous & Flat Landscape
metas.note:
• The Slovak landscape varies between very mountainous and completely flat.
  • Generally speaking, Czechia is hillier, but less mountainous.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Open & Grey Caps
metas.note:
• The top of Slovak sign posts are typically either open, have a grey metal cap or a thin black cap.

--- NOTE:

  • Most Czech sign posts have a thick black cap.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Pair Poles
metas.note: • Slovakia and Czechia most commonly use wide, round concrete poles, which are quite often attached in pairs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Railway Crossing
metas.note:
• The Slovak railway crossing sign has a white rectangular background.

--- NOTE:

  • Czech railway crossing signs do not have a background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Special B-Type Guardrails
metas.note:
• Slovakia and Czechia both use a special kind of type B guardrail, which is wider than the normal type.
  • No other European countries use the same kind.

--- NOTE:

  • While Czechia uses this type fairly consistently, Slovakia also uses other types occasionally.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - Wooden Poles
metas.note:
• It is somewhat more common to see wooden poles, and in turn, white concrete supports in Slovakia rather than in Czechia.

--- NOTE:

  • Because there are many variables, it may sometimes be inconsistent.
  • Therefore, this information should preferably be used to help decide between a difficult fifty-fifty.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - A-Type Guardrails
metas.note:
• Slovenia uses a regular A-type guardrail, like most European countries.
  • This guardrail type has rounded edges.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mostly useful for 50-50s with Croatia, which uses B-type guardrails.
  • This type has square edges.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Architecture
metas.note:
• Slovenian architecture takes much inspiration from alpine architecture, with light coloured walls, dark wooden details and semi-steep roofs.
  • The most common roof shape is half-hipped roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Bollards
metas.note:
• Slovenian bollards are white with a black top.
  • The front reflector will typically be bright red, while the back reflector will be white.

--- NOTE:

  • Austrian bollards have the same design, but with a dark red front reflector and a black or grey back reflector.
  • Montenegrin bollards also have a very similar design, also with a red and a white reflector.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Hilly Landscape
metas.note: • The Slovenian landscape is generally very hilly and forested, with occasional agriculture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - House Numbers
metas.note:
• Slovenian house numbers are typically red with white text.

--- NOTE:

  • Czech house numbers are also commonly red.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Kilometre Markers
metas.note:
• Slovenian kilometre markers have a very distinct design.
  • At the top left the road number is shown in a yellow rectangle, and a second number is to the right of it.
  • A horizontal black line divides the top and bottom, and the distance is shown below.

--- NOTE:

  • Austrian kilometre markers are blue with a white number.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Long Dashed Outlines
metas.note:
• Slovenian roads commonly feature long outer dashes.

--- NOTE:

  • Neighbouring countries do not frequently use dashed outside lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Bird Poles
metas.note:
• The most common type of pole in South Africa features 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that resemble rows of birds, which is why they are referred to as “bird poles” in the community.

--- NOTE:

  • South Africa has a wide variety of other poles and pole tops.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Chevrons
metas.note:
• South Africa uses white-and-red chevrons.
  • You can find a similar chevron pattern below directional signs.
  • In addition, unique-looking small, thin chevrons with one arrow are common next to roads.

--- NOTE:

  • The thin chevrons can also be found in the other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, and Lesotho.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Gen 2
metas.note:
• Generation 2 coverage is quite common in the country.
