  • It can be recognized by the large circular car blur and the halo-like colour distortion in the sky.

--- NOTE:

  • On the continent of Africa, Generation 2 is only found in South Africa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Gen 4 Car
metas.note:
• All Generation 4 coverage in South Africa was taken by a blue Street View car with a short antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • The best way to recognize this car is by the 1 blue pixel at the back.
  • The antenna is sometimes hidden by the blur.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - High Walls
metas.note: • Suburban houses in and around large cities will often be surrounded by high walls, fences, and gates to deter criminals.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - N & R Roads
metas.note:
Green directional signs with yellow road numbers are also used in Lesotho, Eswatini and Botswana. Here, the format of road numbers is useful:

  • N and R-roads are exclusive to South Africa.
  • A and B-roads are exclusive to Botswana and Lesotho.
  • MR-roads are exclusive to Eswatini.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Roadlines
metas.note:
• On most roads, South Africa utilizes single yellow outer lines and white centre lines.

--- NOTE:

  • The other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, and Lesotho also use single yellow outer lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Roadlines #2
metas.note:
• South Africa occasionally features unique white triple centre lines with 2 solid lines on the outside and a dashed line on the inside.
  • You may also sometimes encounter another unique triple centre line, consisting of two white lines with one yellow line in the middle.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other countries where you will find road lines like these are the other southern African countries of Botswana, Eswatini, and Lesotho.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Autumn & Winter
metas.note:
• A considerable amount of the coverage was made during autumn and winter.
  • Note that more pleasant-looking spring and summer coverage is also not uncommon.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Cars
metas.note:
• Almost all road coverage in South Korea is made with a Generation 3 camera.
  • In most, but not all, of the coverage, the back of the Google car is visible.

You can see three colours:

  • Black, white and silver.
  • The car never has an antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• Utility poles almost always have these pole markings near the bottom, consisting of black and yellow diagonal stripes.

These markings look similar to the ones found in Taiwan. There are however two main differences:

  • In South Korea, the stripes do not reach all the way to the bottom, whereas in Taiwan they do.
  • In South Korea, the stripes are more yellow. In Taiwan, they have more of an orange tint.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Spike Pole
metas.note: • Most poles have a tapered “spike” on top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Bollards
metas.note:
• The standard Spanish bollards have a yellow-orange reflector on the front and two white dots on the back (though the back can also be blank).
  • They are typically hollow.

--- NOTE:

  • Very close to Andorra, you can find a slightly different bollard, which is also used in Andorra itself.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Calle
metas.note: • The Spanish word for street is calle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Chevrons
metas.note:
Spain has two chevrons:

  • Black with white arrows.
  • Blue with white arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southern Europe, black with white chevrons can be found in Italy, Greece and Albania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - French Pole Tops
metas.note:
• “French style” poletops are common in Spain.
  • They are shaped like an upside down triangle, with a horizontal top bar that is curved slightly upwards.
  • They are usually found on top of tall ladder poles or medium sized steel poles.

--- NOTE:

  • As the name suggests, French poletops are also very common in France.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Hunting Signs
metas.note:
• In rural areas you will often find hunting signs.
  • There are two versions, both of which are unique to Spain.
  • One is a simple white sign with a text starting with “coto” and ending in “caza”.
  • The other one has a diagonally divided black and white background.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Ladder Poles
metas.note:
• In Spain, you can find a variety of electricity poles and pole tops.
  • In small towns and sparsely populated rural areas concrete ladder poles and wooden poles are the most common.
  • “Ladder” poles have indents that resemble a ladder, hence the name.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - No Border Signs
metas.note:
• Red borders on road signs extend all the way to the edge of the sign.
  • There is no small white border separating the red part from the edge.

--- NOTE:

  • France, Italy and Portugal have a small white border on the edge of such road signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note:
• Spanish pedestrian crossing signs have 8 stripes.
  • This is the highest number of stripes in Europe, and almost unique to Spain.

--- NOTE:

  • The only other European country with 8 stripes is Andorra.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Pylon Supports
metas.note: • High voltage electricity lines supported by pylons are very common in Spain, especially compared to other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Road Markers
metas.note:
• Spain has distinct road markers with a variety of colourful borders.
  • The code on top is the number of the road.

--- NOTE:

  • Andorra has similar markers and the letter codes preceding the road number on these markers are often an important region-specific clue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Rural Dashed Outlines
metas.note:
• Rural roads sometimes have dashed outer lines.
  • This can help tell Spain apart from Portugal and Italy, where such road lines are (almost) non-existent.

--- NOTE:

The reverse is not true:

  • Like Italy and Portugal, many Spanish roads do have solid outer lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Small Font Stop
metas.note:
• Spanish stop signs have a distinct small font.

--- NOTE:

  • These are mostly useful to distinguish Portugal from Spain.
  • Portuguese stop signs have a noticeably larger font.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Yellow Reflectors
metas.note:
• Spain has yellow reflectors on rounded A-type guardrails.

--- NOTE:

  • Belgium, Andorra and Gibraltar also have yellow reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Bollards
metas.note:
• These short, wide stone bollards are unique to Sri Lanka.
  • They have a tapered shape, with a black base and a white top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Gen 3 French Car
metas.note:
In most Generation 3 coverage, you will be able to see the front of the Google car partially through the blur:

  • It is visible as blue-white-red patches, reminiscent of the French flag.
  • The red patch is usually most visually distinct.

--- NOTE:

  • This car is unique to Sri Lanka.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Gen 4 Lowcam
metas.note:
• All Generation 4 coverage is low-cam.

This can be recognized in two ways:

  • The car blur is significantly bigger.
  • Roads look wider and objects around you are seen from a lower angle.

--- NOTE:

  • Sri Lanka’s Generation 3 coverage is made with a normal height camera!
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - License Plates
metas.note: • Vehicles in Sri Lanka have long white front plates and short yellow rear plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: • Throughout Sri Lanka, you will very commonly see insulators that look like mushrooms.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Rural roads often have outside lines, but no middle lines.
  • In the absence of other clues, this can sometimes be a way to decide a tough 50-50.

--- NOTE:

  • Most small roads lack road lines entirely.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Shitcam
metas.note:
• Google used a weird, low-quality camera in Sri Lanka.
  • This camera is known as the official Ari (or “Shitcam”).
  • It has a wide circular car blur and often somewhat brownish colours.

--- NOTE:

  • Within Asia, India and Cambodia also have shitcam coverage.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Striped Signposts
metas.note:
• Sri Lanka commonly uses black and white striped signposts.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South and Southeast Asia, such signposts are also found in Bangladesh, India and Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Architecture
metas.note: • Houses in the Swedish countryside are most commonly wooden and often painted with a distinct dark red paint, which is almost exclusively found in Sweden, Norway and Finland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Bollards
metas.note:
• Swedish bollards are black-and-white, typically with a grey reflector.
  • Reflectors by intersections are commonly orange instead.
  • They can be either wedge-shaped, round, or thin and curved.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Sweden is the only country in Europe whose chevrons have yellow arrows on a blue background.

--- NOTE:

  • While very rare, yellow on blue chevrons also exist in Luxembourg.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Gen 4 Cars
metas.note:
Generation 4 coverage in Sweden features three Street View cars:

  • A red, a white, and a blue car.
  • Each of the cars can be seen with or without a visible antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • Only the blue car is found in Norway, Finland and Denmark.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Short Dashed Roadlines
metas.note:
• On smaller roads, the outer road lines are white and dashed.
  • They are distinctly shorter than the Norwegian dashed lines.
  • In contrast to Norway and Finland, all road lines are white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Snow Poles
metas.note:
• Snow poles are typically orange, with a tall white reflector slightly above the middle of the pole.
  • Some poles have a second, thinner reflector above the normal one.

--- NOTE:

Finland and Norway both have similar orange snow poles:

  • The reflector on Finnish poles is usually much thinner and very close to the top.
  • Norwegian poles typically have either one or two slightly thinner reflectors, with one commonly being very close to the middle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Unique Roadlines
metas.note:
• The outer road lines on highways look solid from a distance, but are typically divided into small sections with a unique pattern, which is different from the solid lines in Finland and Norway.
  • Road lines in Denmark can have a similar pattern, however the individual sections should be rectangular.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Yellow Road Signs
metas.note:
• Swedish road signs have a red border and a yellow background.

--- NOTE:

  • Finnish road signs have a thin yellow border outside the red one.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Bollards
metas.note:
• Swiss bollards are black-and-white with white or grey reflectors.
  • They can be either wedge-shaped or cylindrical with a rounded top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/switzerland for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Lowcam
metas.note:
• By far the most important way to recognize Switzerland, is that all car coverage is low-cam.
  • This means that the camera on the Google car is intentionally set up lower than in most other countries.

--- THIS CAN BE RECOGNIZED IN TWO WAYS:

  • The car blur is significantly bigger.
  • Roads look wider and objects around you are seen from a lower angle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/switzerland for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Pedestrian Sign
metas.note:
• Swiss pedestrian signs have seven stripes, making it almost unique for Europe.
  • Furthermore, rather than the typical European square shape, the signs appear as tall blue rectangles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/switzerland for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note: • In Generation 3 coverage, you can find this black car with a long antenna and a red brake light in the middle, similar to the one you can see in Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Pole Sticker
metas.note:
• Poles almost always feature these black and yellow diagonal-striped markings that run all the way to the bottom.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar markings can be seen in South Korea.
  • However, the markings are much shorter and do not run all the way to the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Roadlines
metas.note:
--- YELLOW LINES:

  • Roads in Taiwan generally feature double yellow middle lines with single white outer lines.

--- WHITE LINES:

  • Roads with outside white road lines and no middle lines at all are common.
  • In the absence of better clues, this type of road line can be a very good way to identify Taiwan.

--- RED LINES:

  • Red outer lines that indicate no parking are common in Taiwan, especially in cities.
  • This is essentially unique to the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Bollards
metas.note:
• The Thai bollard is square shaped with a pointed top, and has black-and-white stripes.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southeast Asia, these bollards are also found in Cambodia, Laos and Indonesia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Bulky Signposts
metas.note:
• Signposts in Thailand are square and bulky in shape, usually white, and often have the bottom painted black.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southeast Asia, this design is unique to Thailand.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Concrete Roads
metas.note:
• Concrete roads are common in Thailand.
  • They often have a large square shaped pattern.

--- NOTE:

  • In Southeast Asia, these can also be found commonly in the Philippines, and less commonly in Indonesia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Lamp Posts
metas.note: • Thailand has very distinct long, thin lamp posts that hang over the side of the road.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Painted Poles
metas.note: • Street light poles have red-and-black or black-and-white stripes on the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Pole
metas.note:
• Thai poles are square and have small holes running vertically up the pole.

--- NOTE:

  • You will see similar poles in Sri Lanka, Cambodia and Laos.
  • Make sure to look for other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Thailand has yellow middle lines.
  • These middle lines are either solid or dashed lines.

--- NOTE:

  • Malaysia only has white middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Black Car
metas.note:
• The Google car in Tunisia is black with a medium-length, thin antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • The colour of the car is not always perceptible.
  • Make sure to look around for other more helpful clues.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Curbs
metas.note:
• Red and white striped curbs are common in Tunisia.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar curbs are also common in Israel and Palestine.
  • Make sure to look for additional information!
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Direction Signs
metas.note:
• Most direction signs have a white background with towns listed in Arabic and Latin script.
  • The font of the Latin script is usually quite distinctive.

--- NOTE:

  • Many direction signs include the capital Tunis, but this does not necessarily mean you are anywhere near that city.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Follow Cars
metas.note:
• One of the best ways to recognize Tunisia is that, in ~98% of coverage, the Google car is escorted by a follow car.
  • There are several different follow cars and these are four of the most commonly found ones.

--- NOTE:

  • Follow cars can be in front of the street view car, or very far behind.
  • Make sure to pan and zoom if you do not find them immediately.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Tunisia usually has white road lines.
  • Outer road lines can be dashed or solid.

--- NOTE:

  • A few roads in Sfax have yellow middle lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Tunisia - Stop Sign
metas.note:
• Tunisia has a fairly unique stop sign with Arabic and Latin script.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar stop signs can be found in Jordan and the UAE.
  • However, Israel and Palestine use a different unique stop sign with a hand instead of text.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/tunisia for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Apartment Blocks
metas.note: • Tall and somewhat square apartment blocks are very common in Turkey.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollards
metas.note:
• Turkish bollards have a simple design: rectangular, plain white, and with a red reflector on the front.
  • They are thin when seen from the side.

--- NOTE:

  • Romania has similar bollards.
  • However, bollards are relatively rare in Romania.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Turkish chevrons are typically red on white.
  • Beware that there are some other regional variants.
  • Usually, the tip of the arrow does not touch the edge of the chevron.
  • Some chevrons have a neon yellow border.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 3 No Antenna
metas.note: • In the Generation 3 coverage, the Google car never has an antenna.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• A grey pickup truck can be found in some Generation 4 coverage.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar pickup trucks can also be found in Senegal and Kenya.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Gen 4 White Car
metas.note:
• The Generation 4 coverage in Turkey typically features a white Google car.
  • Usually, only a tiny sliver of the back of the car is visible.
  • The car can have a short antenna, or no antenna at all.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The colour of Turkish road lines is somewhat inconsistent.
  • Most roads simply have white road lines.
  • However, it is not uncommon to see yellow road lines.
  • These roads can have fully yellow lines, or a combination of yellow and white lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Salt & Pepper Roads
metas.note: • Many roads have pavement with a grainy “salt and pepper” texture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Stop Sign
metas.note:
• Stop signs have the word “DUR” written on them.
  • This is unique to Turkey.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Uganda - Unique Car
metas.note:
• In all coverage in Kampala, a unique Google car is visible.
  • This car is white with square side mirrors and a boxy look.

--- NOTE:

  • This Google car is only found in Uganda and is unique to the city of Kampala and its outskirts.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uganda for more clues.

metas.name: Ukraine - Bad Road Quality
metas.note:
• On average, Ukraine has some of the worst roads in Europe.
  • Most rural roads have lots of potholes, cracks and warped pavement.
  • This abysmal road quality can really help with tough 50-50s with Russia, which generally has somewhat better roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ukraine for more clues.

metas.name: Ukraine - Red Car
metas.note:
• All coverage in Ukraine is Generation 3.
  • Most of it was made using a red Google car.
  • This car is almost unique to Ukraine.
  • It sometimes has an antenna, and sometimes no antenna.

--- NOTE:

  • You will not find the red Generation 3 car in Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ukraine for more clues.

metas.name: Ukraine - Town Entry Signs
metas.note:
• Ukraine uses white town entry signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Russia usually has blue town entry signs instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ukraine for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Curbs
metas.note:
• Similarly, almost all curbs are striped.
  • They can be either black-and-white, or black-and-yellow.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 3 Car
metas.note:
• In almost all Generation 3 coverage, a white car with visible black roof racks was used.

--- NOTE:

  • The UAE is the only Middle Eastern country where a white Google car can be found.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Black Car
metas.note:
• You can also find regular Generation 4 coverage taken with a black car.
  • The brake light is commonly visible.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar Generation 4 black car can be found in Israel.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Gen 4 Truck
metas.note:
• In Generation 4 coverage, a white pickup truck with a trekker camera was used for much of the coverage.
  • In a lot of the coverage, the truck is completely blurred out.

--- NOTE:

  • A similar truck can be found in Qatar and Oman.
  • In the UAE the antenna at the front of the cabin is on the middle of the car, while in Qatar it is on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Landscape
metas.note: • The UAE typically features a flat desert landscape.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Poles
metas.note:
• Electricity poles in the UAE are mostly made of dark brown wood.
  • The pole tops consist of three insulators, symmetrically attached to a horizontal metal bar.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar poletops can be found in Oman.
  • Jordanian poletops may look similar, but they are usually made of grey concrete, and the insulators are more spaced out.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Reddish Sidewalks
metas.note:
• Houses in residential areas are typically made of light-coloured stone.
  • Reddish stones are often used for sidewalks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Outer roadlines are yellow, middle lines either white or yellow.

--- NOTE:

  • Other Middle Eastern countries, like Jordan, Israel and Oman, also use these lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Unpaved Roads
metas.note: • Although the UAE is a wealthy country, it is not uncommon for residential roads to be unpaved.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Bollards
metas.note:
• The most common bollard in the UK looks like this.
  • It has a rounded shape, with a red reflector on the front and a white one on the back.
  • The base and top are black, with a white stripe in the middle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Cat's Eye
metas.note: • These middle lines, that consist of long dashes with cat’s eyes (reflectors) in the gaps between the dashes, are a good clue for the UK.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Chevrons
metas.note:
• Chevrons are black with white arrows.

--- NOTE:

  • Irish chevrons are black with yellow arrows.
  • French chevrons are blue with white arrows.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Give Way
metas.note:
• UK yield signs feature the phrase “GIVE WAY”.

--- NOTE:

  • Irish yields signs just have the word “YIELD”.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - License Plates
metas.note:
• UK front plates are white, while back plates are yellow.
  • Some plates have a blue strip on the left, but most do not.
  • Additionally, you might see a plate with a green ‘Zero Emissions’ strip.

--- NOTE:

  • Ireland uses white front and back plates, always with a blue strip on the left.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Pole Warning Signs
metas.note:
• The yellow warning stickers on utility poles can be a good way to distinguish between the UK and Ireland.
  • The most important difference is that UK stickers feature a guy getting zapped by a lightning bolt.

--- NOTE:

  • The Irish stickers usually have a lightning bolt, but lack the guy getting zapped.
  • They also often have an extra second rectangular sticker with a black outline, below the lightning bolt.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Double yellow road lines are often found on the sides of marked roads, especially in urban areas.
  • These lines indicate a no stopping zone.

--- NOTE:

  • These lines can also be found in Ireland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Square Metal Gates
metas.note:
• Rural metal gates with square corners are very common in the UK.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mainly useful to distinguish it from Ireland, where similar gates typically have rounded corners.
  • Gates in Northern Ireland also typically have rounded corners.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Warning Signs
metas.note:
• Like most European countries, the UK uses triangular warning signs with a red border and a white background.

--- NOTE:

  • This is mostly useful to distinguish between the UK and Ireland, as Ireland uses diamond-shaped yellow warning signs (being the only European country to do so).

metas.name: United Kingdom - Wooden Poles
metas.note:
• The UK uses wooden poles.
  • Pole steps bolted on the side of the pole are very common.
  • These pole steps are shaped like a series of thin horizontal metal rods.

--- NOTE:

  • Ireland also commonly uses wooden poles with pole steps.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United States of America - No Passing Zone
metas.note: • Triangular yellow signs with the phrase ‘No Passing Zone’ are exclusive to the US.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america for more clues.

metas.name: United States of America - Roadlines
metas.note:
• The US uses yellow middle lines and white outer lines.
  • Double middle lines are the most common.
  • On divided roads, the outer line closest to the median will be yellow, and the other lines will usually be white.

--- NOTE:

  • Double middle lines are less common in Canada, but not rare – use this meta with caution.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america for more clues.

metas.name: United States of America - Rumble Strips
metas.note:
• Interstate highways, US highways, and some state roads have rumble strips in each edge of the road; which are small indentations in the pavement perpendicular to the road.

--- NOTE:

  • Rumble strips may appear in Canada, but are much more rare.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america for more clues.

metas.name: United States of America - Speed Limit
metas.note:
• The US uses the phrase ‘Speed Limit’ on their speed signs.

--- NOTE:

  • Canada uses the word ‘Maximum’ on their speed signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states-of-america for more clues.

metas.name: United States Virgin Islands - Unique Car
metas.note: • Car coverage on the islands will have a large, visible street view car, which will either be red or white.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Black Car
metas.note:
• Uruguay only has Generation 3 coverage.
  • Coverage was taken by a black Google car without an antenna.
  • The car is not always visible.

--- NOTE:

  • Within South America, you can also find this car in Argentina and Peru.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Bollards
metas.note: • These white bollards, with one side often painted yellow, and stone barriers, are specific to Uruguay.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Landscape
metas.note:
This is the stereotypical Uruguay round:

  • The coverage often, but not always, features overcast weather.
  • Most of the landscape consists of open grasslands with gentle hills.
  • Occasionally, you might see separated tree plantations.
  • Roads are generally in worse condition than in neighbouring countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Roadlines
metas.note:
• Uruguay often has these triple road lines, that consist of double yellow roadlines with white dashes in between.
  • This is a design not seen anywhere else in the Americas.

➖➖➖➖➖

You can also find two other, non-unique road line patterns:

  • Yellow-white lines (also found in Argentina)
  • Simple white lines (found in many other places).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Thick Signposts
metas.note:
• Uruguay uses thick wooden signposts, which are typically painted white.
  • They often have up to four rectangular notches at the back of the post.

--- NOTE:

  • Thick wooden signposts can also be seen in Bolivia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uruguay for more clues.

metas.name: Uruguay - Trident Poles
metas.note:
• Uruguay uses a handful of different utility poles.
  • One very common and useful one are the so-called trident poles, which get their name from their distinctive pole tops with three insulators that point upwards.

--- NOTE:

  • These trident poles are not found in neighbouring Argentina and Brazil.
